items.title: Announcing: Azure Boost observability for NVMe disks
items.description:
Azure Boost observability for NVMe disks is an open-source command-line tool that you run inside compatible Azure VMs. Backed by Azure Boost, the tool provides remote disk I/O and latency metrics and maps each disk inside your VM to the corresponding disk shown in the Azure portal. This helps you investigate remote disk performance and associate metrics with the right disk.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Immutable snapshots for Azure Disk Storage
items.description:
Immutable snapshots for Azure Disk Storage are now available in public preview. Immutable snapshots complement Azure Backup immutable vaults. Use vaults for cost-efficient long-term retention, and immutable snapshots for short-term backups that need faster restore.

Snapshots are read-only after creation, and you can apply an immutability policy to existing snapshots of any Azure disk type to prevent deletion for up to 90 days. While the policy is active, no one can delete the snapshot, regardless of role or permissions. This helps protect your backups from accidental or malicious deletion and supports regulatory data retention requirements. You can still restore disks, copy snapshots to other regions, and perform all other snapshot operations. Choose between two types of immutability policies:
  1. Unlocked policies let authorized users test a policy before locking it. Authorized users can extend, shorten, or remove an unlocked policy.
  2. Locked policies provide compliance-grade protection. They can only be extended. No one, including administrators and Azure, can shorten or remove them, so the snapshot can't be deleted until the retention period ends. Use them to protect backups from ransomware, meet regulatory requirements for short-term backups that need fast restore, and guard against rogue AI agent behavior.
There's no additional charge for immutability policies; protected snapshots continue to be billed at standard managed disk snapshot rates until you delete them. 

Learn more:

  • Pricing page
  • Documentation

items.title: Generally Available: Cobalt 200 Arm-based Dplsv7, Dpsv7, Epsv7, Mpsv4, and Lpsv5-series Virtual Machines
items.description:
The general purpose Dpsv7 and Dplsv7, memory-optimized Epsv7, high-memory Mpsv4, and dense storage Lpsv5 VMs are now generally available. These virtual machines deliver significant enhancements over the previous generation Cobalt 100 VMs, offering improved CPU performance, greater scalability, and expanded configuration options to meet the demands of a wide range of workloads.

Key improvements include up to:
  • 50% improvement in CPU performance (workload dependent)
  • 20% improvement in remote storage IOPS with NVMe
  • 10% better remote storage throughput with NVMe
  • 15% improvement in network bandwidth
Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Intel and AMD v6 with temp disk for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
items.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server is announcing the general availability of Intel and AMD v6 compute tiers with local temporary disk. The new v6 generation expands the Flexible Server compute portfolio with higher performance, larger scale, and improved price/performance while retaining local temporary disk for workloads that benefit from it.  

You can select the latest v6 Intel and AMD compute options based on your workload requirements while continuing to use the familiar PostgreSQL Flexible Server experience.   

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Intel and AMD v5 diskless tier for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
items.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server is announcing the general availability of Intel and AMD V5 diskless compute. These new options expand the v5 compute portfolio with General Purpose and Memory Optimized SKUs that do not include local temporary SSD.  

If your workloads don’t require local temporary storage, you can select these diskless v5 configurations while retaining the PostgreSQL Flexible Server experience. The new options include Intel and AMD-based compute families across General Purpose and Memory Optimized tiers.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Cobalt 200 compute for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
items.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server is announcing the general availability of Cobalt 200 ARM-based compute. Cobalt 200 expands the Flexible Server compute portfolio with Microsoft-designed ARM64-based compute, giving you an additional architecture choice alongside Intel and AMD x64-based compute.  

With Cobalt 200, you can choose the compute architecture that best fits your PostgreSQL workload, compatibility, and infrastructure requirements.   

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Geo-redundant backup and restore for Azure HorizonDB
items.description:
Geo-redundant backup and restore for Azure HorizonDB is now available. You can use geo-redundant backups to strengthen data protection and restore your HorizonDB deployment in another Azure region when needed.  

With this capability, you have an additional recovery option for scenarios that require cross-region recovery, helping you improve business continuity and disaster recovery preparedness. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Customize backup retention from 1 to 35 days in Azure HorizonDB
items.description:
You can now configure backup retention for your Azure HorizonDB deployments from 1 to 35 days, giving you greater flexibility to align backup retention with your application and data protection requirements.  

Choose the retention period that best fits your workload and recovery needs while Azure HorizonDB manages backups for you.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Throughput buckets in Azure Cosmos DB
items.description:
We're excited to announce the general availability of throughput buckets in Azure Cosmos DB. You can manage the resource consumption of multiple workloads using the same container by limiting the maximum throughput a workload can consume. 

You may need to manage workload throughput consumption in scenarios like:

  1. Multitenant workloads managed by Independent Software Vendors (ISVs).

  2. Bulk execution in ETL jobs.

  3. Data ingestion and migration processes.

  4. Change feed processing.

You can create throughput buckets in a Cosmos DB container using Data Explorer in the Azure portal.

Learn more.

items.title: Limited Preview: AI model management in Azure HorizonDB
items.description:
AI model management in Azure HorizonDB is now in limited preview, designed to simplify how you bring AI into your database. With just a single step, you can provision fully managed AI models for embeddings, semantic ranking, and generation through Microsoft Foundry, without having to manage endpoints, credentials, or cross-service configuration.  

This integrated experience removes the need for manual setup and context switching, allowing you to use built-in AI functions directly within PostgreSQL and immediately start building AI-powered applications. You also gain a unified environment where model provisioning, management, monitoring, and billing are handled seamlessly within Azure HorizonDB, helping you stay focused on your application logic instead of infrastructure complexity. 

The same in-database experience extends to existing models you've already deployed in Microsoft Foundry, streamlining registration while providing full integration with AI functions. 

To request access, complete the AI Model Management limited preview participation form. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Semantic Reranker in Azure Cosmos DB
items.description:
Semantic Reranker in Azure Cosmos DB improves search relevance by reordering candidate results based on the meaning of the search text and surrounding context. It uses an AI model to evaluate candidate documents and promote the ones that best match the intent of a query or natural language question, helping you deliver more accurate, context-aware answers in search and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) scenarios. 

With Semantic Reranker in Azure Cosmos DB, you can add semantic reranking as a dedicated AI step in retrieval workflows for RAG and agent applications. This helps reduce the need to build and tune custom ranking pipelines while keeping Azure Cosmos DB as the operational data store for search and retrieval experiences. 

 Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Pod Sandboxing kata-vm-isolation-v2 runtime class
items.description:
Isolated pods should not force a tradeoff between security and startup performance. With classic sandboxed pod flows, every pod boots a new Kata VM, which adds cold-start latency and extra memory overhead before your app begins work.

The new kata-vm-isolation-v2 runtime class changes that default. It creates pods from a pre-initialized sandbox VM template instead of booting each sandbox from scratch, reduces per-pod memory overhead, and uses Kata’s Rust runtime for better efficiency. You keep strong pod-level VM isolation while getting faster starts and lower runtime cost for sandboxed workloads.

Learn more.

items.title: Pulic Preview: Azure Elastic SAN Next Generation
items.description:
Azure Elastic SAN Next Generation is now in public preview. Elastic SAN Next Generation keeps the core benefits customers value in Elastic SAN today: a single SAN resource hierarchy to consolidate block storage workloads and dynamically share performance, simplifying storage management and lowering total cost of ownership at scale. As a cloud SAN offering, Elastic SAN supports SAN migrations such as datacenter exits and hardware refreshes through iSCSI connectivity, along with the scale needed for cloud-native workloads.

Next Generation builds on that foundation to support mission-critical workloads and advanced storage capabilities such as thin provisioning and autoscaling, helping customers further optimize storage costs while expanding Elastic SAN's fit across SAN migrations and cloud-native applications.

Run mission-critical and general-purpose workloads on the same SAN with noisy-neighbor protection.

Quality of service (QoS) tiers at the volume-group level let customers match performance to workload requirements:

  • Business Critical: Reserved performance with low sub-millisecond latency, up to 400,000 IOPS and 10,000 MBps per volume. Built for SAP HANA, Epic, and I/O-intensive OLTP.
  • General Purpose - Direct Attach: Shared performance with sub-millisecond latency, up to 80,000 IOPS and 2,000 MBps per volume. Built for vector and OSS databases.
  • General Purpose - iSCSI: Shared performance with low single-digit millisecond latency, up to 80,000 IOPS and 1,280 MBps per volume. Built for external storage needs such as Azure VMware Solution (AVS) or customers who prefer iSCSI connectivity.

Efficient provisioning for lower storage TCO

Provision for workload growth without paying for the full logical capacity of volumes upfront, while scaling capacity and performance independently:

  • Thin provisioning: Size volumes for anticipated growth while consuming physical capacity as data is written, up to 5x the SAN's provisioned capacity.
  • Autoscaling: Automatically add SAN capacity based on customer-defined thresholds.
  • Independent capacity and performance provisioning: Provision capacity, IOPS, and throughput independently at the SAN level.
  • Thin clones (coming soon): Create space-efficient, mountable dev/test copies of Business Critical volumes.
  • Crash-consistent snapshots: Protect volumes with point-in-time snapshots.

    A Next Generation SAN can scale up to 1 PiB, 4 million IOPS, and 160 GBps. 

    Sign up for Azure Elastic SAN Next Generation preview.

items.title: Limited Preview: Azure Workload Center for SAP and Azure Copilot Run SAP Agent
items.description:
Azure Workload Center for SAP, together with the Azure Copilot Run SAP Agent, is a workload-aware experience, powered by Workload Virtual Instance (WVI) for operating SAP workloads on Azure. Azure Workload Center for SAP helps teams understand workload health, identify configuration deviations, and assess the impact of platform issues in the context of the SAP systems they support.

Each workload is represented as a Workload Virtual Instance (WVI), bringing architecture, dependencies, metadata, and operational context into a single view. Workload-specific details, such as SAP system identifiers (SIDs) and production designations, help teams and AI agents understand each environment in context, while Azure Monitor health models provide health insights across application, database, and infrastructure layers. 

Customers can discover and onboard workloads, validate configurations against SAP-specific best practices, detect deviations, monitor health, troubleshoot issues, and take guided remediation actions. Purpose-built AI agents help operators understand what changed, assess impact, and identify recommended next steps while keeping teams in control of decisions and remediation. 

Availability: Australia East, Central US, East US, East US 2, Germany West Central, Italy North, Japan East, Korea Central, North Europe, South Central US. 

To sign up for this Limited Preview, please fill out this form.  

Learn more: 

  • Limited Preview of Microsoft Azure Workload Center for SAP | Tech Community Blog 

  • Azure Workload Center for SAP | Microsoft Learn

items.title: Limited Preview: Azure Workload Center for Oracle and Azure Copilot Run Oracle Agent
items.description:
Azure Workload Center for Oracle, together with the Azure Copilot Run Oracle Agent, is a workload-aware experience, powered by Workload Virtual Instance (WVI) for operating Oracle workloads on Azure. Azure Workload Center for Oracle helps teams understand workload health, identify configuration deviations, and assess the impact of platform issues in the context of the applications they support. 

Each workload is represented as a Workload Virtual Instance (WVI), bringing architecture, dependencies, metadata, and operational context into a single view. Workload-specific details, such as Oracle system identifiers (SIDs) and production designations, help teams and AI agents understand each environment in context, while Azure Monitor health models provide health insights across application, database, and infrastructure layers. 

Customers can discover and onboard workloads, validate configurations against workload-specific best practices, detect deviations, monitor health, troubleshoot issues, and take guided remediation actions.   • Azure Workload Center for Oracle | Microsoft Learn

items.title: Public Preview: Database Agent for SQL with contextual Copilot
items.description:
Database Agent now gives you AI-generated, evidence-grounded recommendations for detected database issues, including why the issue matters, the likely cause, and the recommended next step. 

Recommendations draw on available issue evidence and Microsoft-authored scenario knowledge. They distinguish observed evidence from AI-generated conclusions and communicate uncertainty when evidence is incomplete, stale, or conflicting. Recommendations are presented for your review before any state-changing action. 

Learn more.

products: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines
items.title: Generally Available: Database Hub real-time performance dashboards
items.description:
Database Hub in Microsoft Fabric gives you built-in, real-time performance dashboards for Microsoft SQL, Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server, and Azure Cosmos DB in one place. From the Performance page, you can track CPU, memory, storage, IO, connections, and other key signals across your database estate, then drill into the servers and accounts that need attention. Your databases stay where they are, in Azure or on-premises, with no data movement, mirroring, or monitoring infrastructure to set up.

This helps you spot and investigate performance issues across database engines without switching between portals and tools. For Microsoft SQL, you can also create custom monitors from templates as Fabric Real-Time Dashboards and share them with your team. Database Hub uses your existing Microsoft Entra ID and Azure RBAC permissions, and it doesn't require Fabric capacity to access.

Learn more.

items.title: Private Preview: Azure DH/EHasv8 VMs based on 6th Gen AMD EPYC™ (“Venice”) processors
items.description:
We are announcing the preview of the new Azure DHasv8, DHalsv8 and EHasv8-series virtual machines (VMs), powered by 6th Generation AMD EPYC™ (“Venice”) processors. Designed for the next generation of cloud applications, these VMs deliver expanded compute and memory scalability, enhanced storage and networking performance, and flexible configurations to support demanding enterprise, database, and abroader range of AI workloads. 

The preview includes general purpose (DHasv8-series & DHalsv8-series) and memory-optimized (EHasv8-series) VMs, available with and without local disks.

Key enhancements include expanded VM sizes up to 480 cores to support diverse workload requirements; increased memory capacity of up to 3.8 TiB on the EHasv8-series for memory-intensive workloads; and up to 2x higher remote storage IOPS and networking bandwidth on the largest VM sizes compared to the previous generation.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure SQL DB Hyperscale Cross Database Querying
items.description:
Native cross-database queries in Azure SQL Database Hyperscale let applications access and join data across databases in the same Hyperscale elastic pool on a logical server, using familiar T-SQL three-part names such as `database.schema.object`. 

This enables cross-database reporting, shared reference data, and remote stored procedure calls without copying data, consolidating databases, or configuring external tables. Importantly, it unblocks SQL Server migration scenarios that depend on cross-database queries, reducing the need for query rewrites and application redesign when moving to Azure SQL Database. Applications retain separate databases with permissions enforced in each, while transactions can read across multiple databases and write to one database per transaction.

This capability is available in a limited preview, and customers must sign up to participate.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Near-instant provisioning for Azure DocumentDB clusters
items.description:
Now the M10 to M30 computer tiers are available for near-instant provisioning.   

Historically, the free tier in Azure DocumentDB was made available for instant provisioning. The goal was to help you get started without having to wait for 10-15 minutes for clusters to become available. In addition, AI agents don’t have to spend cycles waiting for cluster provisioning before you can kick off a wave of experimentation.  

Now you and your agents can use the popular M10 tier for basic functional testing and experimentation. You can continue to use the M30 as the staple entry point for production-tier applications as you begin your journey on Azure DocumentDB before scaling to higher clusters tiers as you grow.   

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Confidential VMs with OS Disk Encryption support on AKS
items.description:
Regulated customers running AKS Confidential VM node pools protect workloads in memory today, but the OS disk isn't encrypted at rest, so they have to close the data-at-rest gap outside the platform. In Preview, Ubuntu 26.04 Confidential VM node pools enable OS Disk Encryption by default on both Intel TDX and AMD SEV-SNP SKUs, so the OS disk is protected with a CVM-bound key from first boot. Confidential workloads get end-to-end confidentiality (memory and OS disk) without new configuration, new API surface, or changes to existing tooling.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Confidential VMs with Intel TDX support on AKS
items.description:
Customers standardized on Intel Trust Domain Extensions (TDX) for attestation and hardware confidentiality can't run those workloads on AKS Confidential VM node pools today, because CVM node images only support AMD SEV-SNP.

AKS Confidential VM node pools add Intel TDX support alongside AMD SEV-SNP, and the correct CVM image is selected automatically from the VM SKU. Intel-first customers can now bring their confidential workloads to AKS without changing their attestation model, and without any new AKS configuration or API surface. Generally available with Azure Container Linux. Supported with Ubuntu 26.04 preview.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Private endpoint support for Azure HorizonDB clusters
items.description:
You can now connect to Azure HorizonDB clusters privately through Azure Private Link, using a private IP address from your virtual network. Private DNS integration makes connection setup easier, while the option to disable public access keeps database traffic off the public internet.   

Connections are supported from: 

  • Azure virtual networks. 

  • Peered networks. 

  • On-premises environments through VPN or Azure ExpressRoute.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Service tags for inbound rules in network security perimeter
items.description:
Announcing the public preview of 'service tags as inbound rules' support for third-party customers in network security perimeter. 

This new capability simplifies how customers manage access to in network security perimeter-protected resources by allowing them to use service tags as part of network security perimeter access rules when connecting to supported third-party services. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Perimeter link (cross perimeter) in network security perimeter
items.description:
This capability enables secure connectivity between resources protected by different network security perimeters, while maintaining strong perimeter-based access controls. 

With this release, customers can confidently adopt network security perimeter across complex, distributed application architectures that require controlled communication across security perimeters. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Agent Grid helping secure AI agent communications
items.description:
Agent Grid is now in public preview, bringing identity-based Zero Trust network security to AI agents on supported Azure environments. Security teams can govern communications among agents, models, tools, and external services through centrally managed policies. Enforcement operates outside the agent’s trust boundary, without agent code changes or customer-managed sidecars. 

Preview capabilities include TLS inspection, fully qualified domain name (FQDN) filtering, URL filtering, granular Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool filtering, and Azure Content Safety integration for Prompt Shields. Administrators can allow specific tools on an approved MCP server while blocking sensitive operations, restrict outbound destinations, and inspect supported content for prompt-injection attacks. 

Agent Grid applies common policies across onboarded ACI Agent Groups, AKS Agent Sandbox using Kata Containers, and native Kubernetes workloads on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS). Verified workload identities, mutually authenticated encrypted connectivity, and centralized enforcement visibility help security teams protect agent workflows across supported hosting environments. 

Learn more:

  • Documentation
  • Announcement blog

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Adaptive Virtual Patching
items.description:
Azure Adaptive Virtual Patching introduces an AI-orchestrated Adaptive Shield designed to reduce exposure to new, emerging, and newly disclosed zero-day vulnerabilities while customers test and deploy software patches. The initial workload focus is Linux Virtual Machines (VM) and Virtual Machine Scale Sets (VMSS) on Azure. 

The service connects three semantic layers: a knowledge graph of vulnerabilities and exploit conditions, a map of the customer’s actual workloads and runtime context, and an orchestration layer that identifies relevant exposure and generates workload-specific mitigations. AI-synthesized policies use explicit matching conditions and enforcement actions, combining adaptive reasoning with deterministic runtime enforcement. The Adaptive Shield architecture coordinates eBPF-based workload protection and network-based compensating controls to address relevant attack paths. 

Customers onboard workloads as Protected Resources. A workload extension collects telemetry and deploys mitigations directed by the service’s AI core, helping protection adapt as threats and workload conditions change. Azure Adaptive Virtual Patching complements existing security investments and gives customers time to patch safely. It applies temporary mitigations rather than installing software fixes; the corresponding mitigations can be rolled back after patching and confirmed remediation. 

Learn more:

  • Documentation
  • Announcement blog

items.title: Public Preview: AI Security add-on for Azure Firewall Premium
items.description:
AI Security, a new add-on for Azure Firewall Premium, is now in public preview. Announced at Microsoft Ignite, it introduces five capabilities to help you protect AI applications, safeguard sensitive data, strengthen malware and application defenses, and simplify firewall policy management. 

Prompt injection protection uses Azure AI Content Safety Prompt Shields to detect and block prompt-injection attempts in selected traffic, without per-application SDK integration.  

Network DLP integrates with Microsoft Purview to help prevent sensitive corporate data from being uploaded to destinations your organization does not sanction, including AI applications and models.  

Malware detection and application vulnerability protection bring purpose-built small language models (SLMs), fine-tuned for network security and optimized to run on CPUs, into inline inspection. These models analyze binary files and application requests in transit to detect malware and exploit attempts, enabling policy enforcement before identified threats reach their destinations. 

AI policy combines firewall configuration with observed network traffic to provide contextual insights and recommendations. Use these insights to review unused rules, identify opportunities to improve rule order, and investigate traffic anomalies. Review recommendations and validate changes with a dry-run before applying them.  

Together, these capabilities bring AI-powered intelligence to network protection and policy management. 

Learn more:

  • Documentation
  • Announcement blog

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Bastion RDP and SSH vision
items.description:
Azure Bastion RDP and SSH vision is now in public preview, bringing AI-assisted review to recorded privileged sessions. Security and operations teams can use session summaries and insights into noteworthy and risky activity to understand administrative actions and focus investigations, reducing the need to review every recording from beginning to end. 

Vision turns session recordings into investigation insights across RDP and SSH, with full SSH command logs providing additional detail for command review. Teams can prioritize sessions for follow-up and use the underlying recordings to assess context, helping make privileged-access audits and investigations more efficient. 

The capability builds on Azure Bastion Premium session recording, with recordings stored in the customer’s designated Azure Storage account. Vision extends the value of these recordings with AI-assisted analysis to support clearer oversight of privileged activity. 

Learn more:

  • Documentation
  • Announcement blog

items.title: Public Preview: Agent Sandbox cluster extension
items.description:
Running AI agents that execute untrusted, model-generated code requires isolated environments for each session. Today, teams building on Kubernetes assemble their own sandbox lifecycle, storage, and warm-up logic, adding operational overhead and making users wait while fresh environments initialize.  

We’re introducing the Agent Sandbox cluster extension. Built on the open-source Kubernetes Agent Sandbox project, the managed extension provides declarative sandbox creation, lifecycle management, and pre-warmed pools. Together, Agent Sandbox cluster extension and Pod Snapshot cluster extension enable isolated agent environments to be snapshotted and restored while preserving runtime state across the sandbox lifecycle.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Scale ExpressRoute Direct connectivity with link groups
items.description:
Azure ExpressRoute is introducing link groups for ExpressRoute Direct, enabling high-throughput workloads to scale network connectivity while reducing operational complexity. Instead of managing multiple independent ExpressRoute connections, you can aggregate multiple physical links into a single logical connection.

With link groups, you can:

  • Scale connectivity capacity by grouping multiple ExpressRoute Direct links into a single logical connection.
  • Improve resiliency with Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP), including dynamic link negotiation and failover.
  • Simplify operations by managing aggregated connectivity and monitoring at the group level instead of operating independent connections.
  • Customize availability behavior by configuring the minimum number of active links required for the group to remain operational.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure API Management Application
items.description:
The Applications feature in Azure API Management is now available in public preview to all customers, with no sign-up or registration required.

Applications provide a streamlined way to organize APIs around consuming applications and manage application-level access. API providers can register applications, associate them with API products, and use Microsoft Entra ID to enable secure, identity-based API consumption.

With Applications, organizations can:

  • Simplify application onboarding: Register and manage API-consuming applications directly in Azure API Management.
  • Enable identity-based access: Use Microsoft Entra ID and OAuth 2.0 client credentials to authenticate applications accessing APIs.
  • Streamline API authorization: Associate applications with products to control access to APIs.
  • Improve developer experience: Provide a centralized experience for managing applications and API access.

items.title: Public Preview: Windows Trusted Launch
items.description:
Teams running Windows workloads on AKS often need stronger boot-chain protection for regulated or security-sensitive environments, but Trusted Launch support has historically stopped short of Windows node pools. With Windows Server 2025, AKS will preview Trusted Launch for Windows nodes, adding Secure Boot and vTPM-backed measured boot so the underlying VMs can verify signed boot components and surface boot integrity signals. Platform teams get a more trusted Windows host baseline for Kubernetes workloads, reducing exposure to bootkits, rootkits, and low-level malware without leaving the AKS node pool model.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: User-assigned managed identity for Azure HorizonDB
items.description:
User-assigned managed identity (UMI) support is now generally available for Azure HorizonDB, enabling you to assign and centrally manage Azure identities for your HorizonDB clusters. With UMI, you can reduce the need to manage credentials for secure access to Azure resources.


You can use UMIs with supported HorizonDB capabilities, including customer-managed keys (CMK) and Microsoft Entra authentication, helping you build more secure integrations while reducing the operational burden of managing credentials.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Microsoft Entra authentication for Azure HorizonDB
items.description:
Microsoft Entra authentication is now generally available for Azure HorizonDB, providing a more secure, identity-based approach to database authentication. You can use Microsoft Entra authentication to centrally manage identities and access instead of relying solely on locally managed database passwords, helping you reduce credential-management overhead and strengthen your security posture.  

Microsoft Entra authentication is the recommended authentication approach for HorizonDB. You can use Microsoft Entra authentication exclusively for stronger protection against password-based risks or enable it alongside HorizonDB password authentication when you still require local credentials.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Database for MySQL on Premium SSD v2
items.description:
Azure Database for MySQL now supports Premium SSD v2 (managed disks) in public preview. Premium SSD v2 provides higher performance and better price-performance compared to Premium File Share, with the flexibility to independently scale storage capacity, IOPS, and throughput. This update enables you to optimize costs and performance based on your workload requirements, from steady-state applications to bursty, transaction-intensive workloads.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB full-text search BM25 score projection
items.description:
Azure Cosmos DB full-text search now includes BM25 score projection, giving you clear visibility into why results appear in the order they do. Your app can now access the relevance score for each result directly, making search ranking more transparent.

This new capability helps you display relevance, troubleshoot unexpected ordering, and tune ranking with confidence. You can also compare how different ranking signals contribute to final relevance, helping you build better search experiences on top of your Azure Cosmos DB data.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Managed Redis database integration guidance
items.description:
Improved database integration guidance for Azure Managed Redis helps you add caching to applications built with Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server, Azure Cosmos DB, and Azure SQL. 

You can use practical guidance, reference architectures, and step-by-step tutorials to implement caching best practices and common patterns. These resources help you reduce database load, improve application responsiveness, and choose the right caching approach for your workload. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Managed Redis keyspace notifications
items.description:
Keyspace notifications are now generally available for Azure Managed Redis, enabling your applications to receive events through pub/sub when data in your cache changes. You can configure the event types that matter to your application and subscribe to notifications for selected keys or operations. 

 These notifications help you build event-driven applications that monitor key changes, respond to expirations, and trigger downstream actions without continuously polling the cache. You can update the notification settings as your application requirements evolve. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Managed Redis agent kit
items.description:
The Azure Managed Redis agent kit makes guidance for building and operating production-ready Redis applications available directly into your AI-assisted development workflows. You get recommendations for caching, messaging, search, AI patterns, client configuration, resilience, and performance, along with Azure-specific guidance for provisioning, networking, security, availability, geo-replication, durability, and observability. 

 The kit helps you make informed design choices, identify configuration issues earlier, and move from development to production with greater confidence. It also connects you to guided workflows for migrating from Azure Cache for Redis and Azure Cache for Redis Enterprise to Azure Managed Redis.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Cache for Redis to Azure Managed Redis migration tooling
items.description:
The general availability of built-in DNS migration tooling simplifies endpoint migration from Azure Cache for Redis Basic, Standard, and Premium tiers to Azure Managed Redis. The tooling lets you redirect the existing cache hostname to an existing Azure Managed Redis instance, allowing applications to reconnect using the same hostname and access key. The tool also supports data retention across migration. 

This built-in tooling reduces immediate application configuration changes and simplifies traffic cutover while you validate the new cache. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: IP filtering in Azure Managed Redis
items.description:
Azure Managed Redis now supports adding firewall rules for accessing data, and it gives you greater control over network access to your caches. You can restrict connections to approved source IP addresses or Azure service tags, helping protect publicly accessible cache endpoints.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Redis 8 in Azure Managed Redis
items.description:
Redis 8 is now available in Azure Managed Redis, bringing the latest Redis innovation to Azure's fully managed Redis service. With richer queries, atomic JSON updates, field-level expiration, and fine-grained security, Redis 8 simplifies development and helps you build sophisticated applications faster. 

With new vector capabilities, you can build AI-powered applications faster for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), semantic search, recommendations, and agent memory. Azure Managed Redis helps you move beyond traditional caching and use Redis as a real-time data layer for modern and AI-driven applications. 

By combining Redis 8 with Azure's enterprise-grade reliability, security, and scalability, you can accelerate application performance, simplify AI architectures, and innovate with confidence on a fully managed service. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Shard-level metrics in Azure Managed Redis
items.description:
Azure Managed Redis now provides shard-level metrics, giving you greater visibility into the performance of individual shards. This added granularity helps you understand workload distribution, identify potential hotspots, and troubleshoot performance more effectively. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure SQL Managed Instance link support for availability groups with multiple databases
items.description:
You can now use a single Azure SQL Managed Instance link to extend a SQL Server Always On Availability Group with multiple databases to Azure SQL Managed Instance. You can extend an existing availability group or create a new one with multiple databases, providing a simpler path to minimum-downtime migrations and disaster recovery in Azure. 

With Managed Instance link, you can continuously replicate your databases to and from Azure and perform bidirectional failovers between supported SQL Server versions and Azure SQL Managed Instance. This enhancement streamlines migration and failover for enterprise applications that rely on multiple related databases running together in the same availability group, giving you greater flexibility to migrate, reverse migrate, or set up disaster recovery in Azure while minimizing application disruption.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Zone-redundant Next-gen GP tier in Azure SQL Managed Instance
items.description:
Zone redundancy for the Next-gen General Purpose service tier helps improve the resiliency of Azure SQL Managed Instance by distributing critical service components across availability zones. This update helps you protect applications against zonal failures while retaining the performance, scalability, and price-performance benefits of Next-gen General Purpose.   

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Backup for Azure Cosmos DB
items.description:
Vaulted backups add an independent protection layer by storing immutable backup copies in an Azure Backup vault, isolated from the source Azure Cosmos DB account, and managed through Azure Backup. This update helps you meet a key requirement of many regulated industries.   

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Embedding generation in Azure Cosmos DB
items.description:
Embedding generation converts content into vector embeddings that capture semantic meaning, helping applications find relevant information beyond exact keyword matches. It uses specialized Azure Data-developed models to support semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).  

With the Azure.Data.AI SDK, you can add embedding generation directly to retrieval workflows for RAG and agent applications through a focused interface.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB SDK for Rust
items.description:
The Azure Cosmos DB SDK for Rust gives you a native Rust client for building applications on Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL. You get access to database operations directly from Rust, with built-in performance optimizations and failure handling. Efficient binary encoding, automatic retries, and partition-level failover and circuit breaking are enabled by default. These capabilities help you build reliable, high-performance applications with less client configuration and custom recovery logic.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Network Watcher – Packet capture insights
items.description:
Packet capture Insights uses AI-assisted analysis to surface key findings from packet captures and can ingest structured protocol logs into log analytics ingestion for deeper investigation. 

Packet capture insights help make capture data more accessible by surfacing meaningful network observations without requiring you to manually inspect every packet. You can use these insights to reduce investigation time, identify abnormal behavior, and troubleshoot connectivity, performance issues more efficiently especially when captures are large or complex. 

Optionally ingesting the derived protocol logs into a Log Analytics workspace preserves structured evidence for deeper investigation, correlation, validation, and repeatable KQL analysis after the insight summary is generated.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Full-text search in Azure DocumentDB
items.description:
You can use full-text search in Azure DocumentDB, in public preview, with BM25 indexing, relevance-based sorting, and access to relevance scores. Fuzzy and proximity search help you handle typos and find documents where search terms occur near one another.  

With support for additional data types and the compound operator for filtering, you can build more expressive search queries over your document data. These capabilities give you greater control over which results are returned and how they are ranked, without deploying a separate search service.   

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: DocumentDB extension for VS Code
items.description:
DocumentDB for VS Code is now generally available. This free, open-source extension brings Azure DocumentDB and the open-source DocumentDB project into Visual Studio Code, supporting any MongoDB API-compatible workload. 

You can connect to Azure DocumentDB clusters, Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB accounts, Kubernetes-hosted databases, MongoDB Atlas, or self-hosted servers. Authentication supports Microsoft Entra ID and managed identity. 

The extension includes a built-in Interactive shell that reuses existing connections, so there is no separate shell to install or configure. You can browse collections; query data in table, tree, or JSON views; use schema-aware autocompletion; and save repeatable scripts in a Query Playground. 

It also supports DocumentDB Local with Docker and sample data, Query Insights for execution plans and statistics, optional GitHub Copilot recommendations, index management, cluster dashboards, and copy-paste migration of collections and indexes between databases or clusters. 

Install it from the Visual Studio Marketplace. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: DocumentDB enabled by Azure Arc
items.description:
With the public preview of DocumentDB enabled by Azure Arc, you can deploy DocumentDB on supported Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes clusters across on-premises, edge, and multicloud environments. Run MongoDB-compatible document workloads where applications and data need to reside, while using Azure Arc for inventory, configuration, and governance of the underlying Kubernetes infrastructure. Built on PostgreSQL, DocumentDB supports familiar MongoDB-compatible APIs and tools.   

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: DocumentDB on Azure Local
items.description:
With the public preview of DocumentDB on Azure Local, you can run MongoDB-compatible document workloads on your own infrastructure. Deploy applications and their data close together to address latency and data-location requirements in datacenters, retail locations, and industrial environments. Built on PostgreSQL, DocumentDB supports familiar MongoDB-compatible APIs and tools, while Azure Local provides the infrastructure platform.   

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Fine-grained role-based access control for databases and collections in Azure DocumentDB
items.description:
Azure DocumentDB now offers granular role-based access control (RBAC) , well beyond the cluster-level permissions that have been offered in the service. You can now use database-level and collection-level RBAC to manage data access. Instead of relying only on cluster-scoped roles, you can create custom roles for a specific database or individual collection and assign the supported data privileges your users and applications require.  

This update gives you greater control over who can access and modify your data, helping you apply least-privilege access across databases, applications, and workloads while keeping permissions scoped to where they are needed.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure HorizonDB now available in 15 regions
items.description:
Azure HorizonDB is expanding to additional Azure regions, giving you greater flexibility to deploy PostgreSQL workloads closer to your applications and users.  

With expanded regional availability, you have more options when choosing where to deploy Azure HorizonDB based on your workload needs. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Managed MCP Server in Azure Cosmos DB
items.description:
We’re announcing the preview of the Azure Cosmos DB hosted MCP experience, enabling enterprise AI agents to securely connect to business data through a standard, managed MCP endpoint. Agents can discover schemas, retrieve documents, and use full-text, vector, and hybrid search to ground responses in relevant, up-to-date data stored in Azure Cosmos DB.  

Because the experience is hosted and managed by Microsoft, you don’t need to deploy, patch, scale, or monitor your own MCP server infrastructure. You can focus on building intelligent, grounded agent experiences while using Azure identity, role-based access controls, and the performance and global scale of Azure Cosmos DB.   

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB Shell
items.description:
We’re excited to announce the general availability of Azure Cosmos DB Shell, a command-line experience that makes it easier for you and for AI agents to work with Azure Cosmos DB.  

Azure Cosmos DB Shell provides a consistent, scriptable workflow for navigating resources, querying and managing data, importing and exporting datasets, and inspecting settings, such as indexing and throughput. You can use the shell from your terminal, in Visual Studio Code, or through the Azure portal. Its MCP integration also enables AI agents to securely interact with Azure Cosmos DB using familiar shell commands.  

Whether you’re exploring data, automating repeatable operations, loading large datasets, or managing application data, Azure Cosmos DB Shell helps you work faster without building custom tooling.   

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview:  AI-assisted data modeler and other updates in Azure Cosmos DB extension for VS Code
items.description:
You can now use the AI-assisted Data Modeler in Visual Studio Code to design an effective Azure Cosmos DB data model earlier in the development lifecycle. It analyzes document structure, query patterns, write distribution, expected scale, and data growth to recommend suitable partition keys and container configurations.  

Recommendations are grounded in Azure Cosmos DB best practices. You can compare alternatives, understand trade-offs, and identify risks such as hot partitions, uneven data distribution, and costly cross-partition queries before deploying. You can then generate an implementation-ready Bicep, Terraform, or SDK configuration without leaving Visual Studio Code. 

 The updated extension also introduces an account dashboard that provides a centralized view of an Azure Cosmos DB account and its resources. You can quickly understand your account, navigate to databases and containers, and access common development workflows from one place.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure SQL Managed Instance updates for mid-November 2026
items.description:
In mid-November 2026, the following updates and enhancements were made to Azure SQL Managed Instance: 

  • Boost transaction throughput in Next-gen General Purpose Azure SQL Managed Instance with increased log rates of up to 220 MiB/s and higher per vCore throughput, improving performance for transaction-intensive workloads.
  • Right-size storage and compute more efficiently in Next-gen General Purpose Azure SQL Managed Instance with improved storage-to-vCore ratios and finer-grained storage scaling, reducing the need to overprovision vCores for storage-intensive workloads.
  • Right-size memory independently of vCores for zone-redundant Next-gen General Purpose Azure SQL Managed Instances, helping optimize performance and resource utilization without overprovisioning compute.

Learn more:

  • New capabilities in Next-gen General Purpose
  • Flexible Memory in Azure SQL Managed Instance

items.title: Generally Available: Azure SQL updates for mid-November 2026
items.description:
In mid-November 2026, the following updates and enhancements were made to Azure SQL:   

  • Fuzzy string matching enables you to compare strings based on similarity rather than relying only on exact matches. Using built-in functions, you can measure the difference or similarity between strings with algorithms such as Damerau-Levenshtein (OSA) and Jaro-Winkler. 
  • Regex-based Dynamic Data Masking extends the built-in DDM feature in Azure SQL Database with flexible, pattern-based masking using regular expressions—centrally enforced at the database layer.
  • AES keys support for Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) with customer-managed keys in Azure SQL Database are now generally available, providing an alternative to RSA keys for protecting data at rest and helping you prepare for the evolving quantum threat landscape. 
  • You can now customize how numeric values appear in the SSMS results grid without changing your queries or Windows regional settings. Choose your preferred digit grouping and decimal symbols, or use your system defaults. A live preview shows how your selections will look, and changes apply to open grids without restarting SSMS or rerunning your query.

Learn more: 

  • Fuzzy string matching
  • Regex-based Dynamic Data Masking
  • AES keys support for Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) with customer-managed keys in Azure SQL Database
  • Customize numeric values

items.title: Public Preview: SQL Server 2025 support on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS
items.description:
Announcing Public Preview support for SQL Server 2025 on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, allowing you to evaluate, test, and deploy SQL Server on Canonical's latest long-term supported platform.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Network Watcher – AI summary of connection troubleshoot results
items.description:
AI-summarized connection troubleshoot results introduces a faster, clearer way to understand connectivity test results in Azure. Connection troubleshoot runs four diagnostic tests, each giving a different view of the network path. Making sense of these results together has required strong networking expertise and manual correlation across tests. With this release, AI does that correlation for customers. 

AI reviews the results of all four tests together and returns a single, easy-to-read summary. The summary states what is happening, the probable cause and how confident the AI is in that cause. It then recommends next steps to resolve the issue. For example, if all probes to a destination fail and the diagnostics show no service listening on the tested port, the summary points to the destination VM as the likely cause. It rates that finding with high confidence and suggests checking the service status and port configuration. 

This enhancement removes the need to interpret and correlate each test's results by hand. Customers get a clear explanation of what went wrong and why, along with practical guidance on what to fix. Teams without deep networking expertise can act on the results themselves, and experienced engineers can confirm the root cause faster. 

By adding AI-powered summaries to connection troubleshoot, Azure helps customers move from raw diagnostic data to a confident, actionable answer in minutes. That makes troubleshooting faster, simpler and more accessible across their Azure workloads. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Network Watcher – Auto-create connection monitor
items.description:
Auto-create connection monitor introduces a new, faster way to set up network monitoring across an entire Azure subscription. Until now, connection monitor tests were created one connection at a time, with each region, source, destination, test configuration and alert set up by hand. That approach gives precise control, but setting up broad coverage takes significant effort. With this release, customers can choose auto-create next to the existing manual option: select a subscription as the scope, and Connection Monitor recommends what to monitor. 

With auto-create connection monitor, the service scans the subscription's resource topology. It discovers Application Gateways, Load Balancers, VPN and ExpressRoute gateways, virtual network and local network gateways, private endpoints and SQL servers. It then recommends the connections most worth monitoring, skips tests that already exist, and explains the reasoning behind each recommendation. Customers can review, filter and edit the recommended tests and see the estimated monthly cost before creating them all in a single step. 

Auto-create complements manual setup instead of replacing it. Customers can use Auto-Create to quickly establish subscription-wide coverage, and keep creating individual tests manually when they need fine-grained control over specific connections. This helps teams reduce blind spots while keeping full transparency and control over every test. 

By adding auto-create to connection monitor, Azure gives customers a choice in how they set up monitoring. They can get broad, reliable coverage in minutes or tailor each test by hand, so connectivity issues are detected earlier and resolved faster across their Azure workloads. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Network Watcher – Connection analyzer
items.description:
Connection analyzer for ExpressRoute Circuit introduces a faster, evidence-based way to find where packet loss occurs on an ExpressRoute circuit. When customers see packet loss between Azure and on-premises today, it is often hard to tell whether the problem lies with the Microsoft Enterprise Edge (MSEE), the connectivity provider, or the customer's own network. That leads to guesswork and long back-and-forth investigations. With this release, customers can pinpoint whether the loss originates at the MSEE. 

Connection analyzer runs on-demand iPerf test traffic from an Azure virtual machine to an on-premises destination over the ExpressRoute circuit, and captures packets at the MSEE. It then reports whether packet loss is occurring at the MSEE and flags out-of-order packet delivery. The full packet capture (pcap) is available to download for deeper analysis. 

This enhancement replaces guesswork with proof. If the loss is at the MSEE, customers have clear evidence to act on. If it isn't, they can quickly focus their investigation on the provider or customer side of the circuit. Built specifically for Azure-to-on-premises traffic, it helps teams narrow down the source of connectivity issues without lengthy manual analysis. 

By bringing packet-level visibility to the Microsoft edge, Azure helps customers isolate ExpressRoute issues faster, shorten time to resolution, and keep their hybrid workloads running reliably. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Network Watcher – Resource health and topology in connection monitor tests
items.description:
Resource health metrics in connection monitor brings resource health and key performance metrics into the Connection Monitor test topology, powered by Network Watcher topology. Until now, the topology showed the path between source and destination, but it didn't show the health of the resources along that path. When a test reported packet loss or high latency, customers had to switch between tabs and blades to check each resource's health and metrics. That slowed down investigations and made it hard to connect the dots. With this release, health and metrics now appear directly in the topology. 

Customers can now click any resource in the connection monitor topology to see its resource health status and time-series metrics in the same view. For example, selecting a load balancer shows its health along with data path availability, health probe status, SNAT connection count and SYN count. Customers can view these metrics alongside connection monitor's own packet loss and latency over the same time window. This makes it easy to see whether a drop in a resource's health lines up with a connectivity issue. 

This enhancement brings loss, latency, health and topology together in one view. When a resource is unhealthy, its metrics are a click away, with no need to switch tabs or tools. Customers can correlate resource health signals with connectivity results to reach the root cause faster. It requires no setup and is available for all new and existing connection monitor tests. 

By surfacing resource health directly in the connection monitor topology, Azure helps customers go from detecting a connectivity issue to understanding its cause faster, so they can resolve problems sooner and keep their workloads running reliably. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Durable Task SDK for Go
Public Preview: Native disaster recovery for Azure Functions durable task scheduler
items.description:
Disaster recovery for Azure Functions durable task scheduler is now available in public preview for the Dedicated SKU in supported Azure regions.

Recover business-critical workflows from regional outages without rebuilding orchestration state, with a repeatable path to resume processing in another region.

Customers can pair a primary scheduler with a passive secondary scheduler in another region. Durable task scheduler replicates orchestration state to the paired scheduler and provides a customer-initiated planned failover operation, reducing the custom recovery engineering required for regulated and mission-critical workloads.

The preview uses an active-passive model. Customers remain responsible for deploying compatible workers, compute, networking, and application dependencies in the secondary region, redirecting application traffic, and initiating scheduler failover through their disaster recovery runbook. Processing resumes from durable checkpoints, and in-progress work might replay or re-execute after failover.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Customer-managed keys for Azure Functions durable task scheduler
items.description:
Customer-managed keys for Azure Functions Durable Task Scheduler are now generally available for Dedicated SKU schedulers.

Organizations that need to manage their own encryption keys can now use customer-managed keys to protect their workflow data, supporting separation of duties, centralized auditing of key access, and customer-defined key rotation policies.

Customers can use a key they own in Azure Key Vault or Azure Managed Hardware Security Module (HSM) to protect scheduler data at rest. Configuration is available through the ARM REST API, Azure CLI using az rest, or Bicep.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Network Watcher VNet Flow Logs enriched with networkInterfaceIP field
items.description:
Azure Network Watcher VNet Flow Logs now provides enhanced capture-side interface context with the networkInterfaceIP field. 

The networkInterfaceIP field records the IP address or addresses of the network interface where a flow was captured, making it easier to identify the resource associated with the captured traffic, determine the next hops in the network traffic flow, and attribute flow records to the correct resource ID. 

This additional context provides greater visibility into how traffic moves through your network, including for interfaces using IPv4 or dual-stack addressing. It helps you trace traffic paths, identify the resources involved at different points in the flow, and simplify network monitoring and troubleshooting. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Network Watcher Private Link support
items.description:
Azure Network Watcher VNet Flow Logs now supports flow log enrichment for Azure Private Link Service, providing greater visibility into network traffic flowing through Private Link Service. 

With this capability, Virtual Network Flow Logs retain backend flow details while adding context about the original source, translated Private Link Service address information, and the Private Link connection identifier. This helps service providers trace connections from the original client, through the Private Endpoint and Private Link Service translation layer, to the backend workload. 

Traffic Analytics also supports this enriched Private Link Service traffic, extending its monitoring and analytics capabilities to Private Link Service scenarios. You can now use Traffic Analytics to visualize traffic patterns, monitor network communication, investigate connectivity and security issues, and gain actionable insights into workloads exposed through Private Link Service. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Network Watcher rule recommendation
items.description:
Azure Network Watcher rule recommendation is now in public preview, helping you proactively identify opportunities to improve network security based on observed network traffic. 

With this capability, you can use Traffic Analytics insights to identify network security rules that may be overly permissive or no longer required. Rule recommendation analyzes observed traffic patterns and provides actionable recommendations to help you strengthen your network security posture while maintaining required connectivity. 

You can review recommendations, drill down into the supporting traffic insights, and use this context to make informed decisions before updating your network security rules. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Functions support for Python 3.15
items.description:
Azure Functions support for Python 3.15 is now in public preview.

Developers can evaluate Python applications, dependencies, native extensions and deployment workflows using the existing v1 and v2 programming models.

Dependency overlap between the Python worker’s gRPC messaging packages and application dependencies can create compatibility conflicts. A new Rust-based transport addresses this by handling host messaging and embedding CPython without depending on the Python grpcio and protobuf packages, reducing dependency overlap and introducing performance benefits. Applications can still use these packages, and existing Python execution libraries continue to run functions. Developers continue writing Python, not Rust.

Planned scope: Linux x64 on Flex Consumption, Elastic Premium and Dedicated (App Service), where each plan is offered.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Functions support for Node.js 26
items.description:
Azure Functions support for Node.js 26 is now in public preview.

Developers can evaluate their JavaScript and TypeScript function apps on the new runtime while continuing to use the Azure Functions programming model on Linux in the Flex Consumption, Elastic Premium, and Dedicated (App Service) plans. Linux Consumption is not supported. Support for Windows hosting plans will roll out in the future.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Golang support on Azure Functions Flex Consumption
items.description:
First-class Go support on Azure Functions Flex Consumption is now generally available.

The Go worker offers a code-first programming model with typed Go handlers, standard Go modules, and integration with Azure Functions Core Tools and Azure CLI. Developers can build HTTP APIs, scheduled jobs, event-processing applications, integration workloads, and durable workflows without introducing a second application language or a custom-handler abstraction.

The release supports Azure Functions triggers, typed batch processing, Blob Storage SDK client injection, and generic registration for compatible extensions. It also includes HTTP streaming, Durable Functions orchestrations and activities, structured logging, and configurable OpenTelemetry export alongside Application Insights host telemetry. Azure Functions Core Tools supports local development, packaging, and deployment.

Unlike the existing custom-handler path for Go, native worker integration removes the need to operate a custom-handler HTTP server or manually author function.json files. The model supports standard net/http handlers and typed event payloads, with host-managed triggers and scaling.

Learn more:
  • Go developer reference
  • Official Go worker
  • Official Go worker releases
  • Official Go worker samples

items.title: Public Preview: Azure App Service Builder
items.description:
Turning application code into a running cloud app often requires developers to configure build pipelines, deployment workflows, and hosting infrastructure. Azure App Service Builder simplifies that journey with a source-connected platform for building, deploying, and running web applications on Azure. Developers and AI coding agents can connect a GitHub repository and deploy a static site, backend web app, or frontend-plus-API application while the service manages the underlying build and hosting infrastructure. Portal, CLI, and guided GitHub Copilot app experience bring deployment into the workflows developers already use.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Private endpoints for Azure Functions durable task scheduler
items.description:
Private endpoints for Azure Functions durable task scheduler are now generally available for both Dedicated and Consumption SKU schedulers. 

Customers can connect Azure Functions and other durable task SDK workloads to a scheduler through a private IP address in their virtual network using Azure Private Link. Traffic remains on the Microsoft backbone instead of traversing the public internet, and customers can disable public network access so the scheduler accepts traffic only through approved private endpoints. 

The private endpoint uses the scheduler's existing endpoint and Microsoft Entra authentication model, allowing applications to adopt private connectivity without changing orchestration code. Customers can configure the capability through the Azure portal, Azure CLI, or Bicep and can connect multiple virtual networks to the same scheduler.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Durable Task extension for Microsoft Agent Framework
items.description:
The Durable Task extension for Microsoft Agent Framework is now generally available for C# and Python. 

Build agents, multi-agent orchestrations, and Microsoft Agent Framework workflows that can run reliably for minutes, days, or weeks. The extension persists agent sessions, checkpoints orchestration and workflow progress, and automatically resumes work after LLM rate limits, network timeouts, process restarts, scale events, or infrastructure failures without requiring custom recovery logic.   

The extension supports two hosting models. Customers can use Azure Functions for managed, serverless hosting with automatic scaling and generated HTTP endpoints, or bring their own compute using containers, Kubernetes, services, or existing application infrastructure. Completed work is preserved and can resume on another worker without losing conversation context or repeating completed steps. 

Key capabilities include persistent conversation history, deterministic multi-agent orchestration, durable Agent Framework graph workflows, human-in-the-loop waits, external events, session time-to-live cleanup, reliable streaming, and visibility through the Durable Task Scheduler dashboard. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Geo-redundancy on Azure App Service
items.description:
Geo-redundancy in Azure App Service, now in public preview, helps customers build more resilient web applications across Azure regions without independently creating and managing an App Service deployment in each region. App Service creates and manages regional application replicas, synchronizes supported application content and configuration, and provides a global endpoint for traffic across regions. Customers can choose Passive mode for regional failover or Active mode to distribute traffic across healthy regions.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Hosted Skill and Agent Bindings for Azure Functions
items.description:
Hosted Skill and Agent bindings for Azure Functions are now available in public preview. Adding agents to an application often requires setup and lifecycle code before developers can focus on business logic. These bindings reduce that plumbing while keeping your function code in control of validation, when agents run, and how results are used.

Choose from three approaches:

  • Hosted Skill Binding: Invoke Markdown-defined hosted skill through a simple API without working directly with the underlying agent SDK. Reuse skill configuration, tools, and conversation history, with support for streaming results and continuing conversations.

  • Microsoft Agent Framework Agent Binding: Work directly with a native Microsoft Agent Framework agent, including SDK APIs, your own model client, and custom Python tools.

  • GitHub Copilot Agent Binding: Work directly with a native GitHub Copilot SDK session, including its session APIs, hostools, and configuration options.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: OS-level dependency support via containers for Azure Functions Flex Consumption
items.description:
OS-level dependency support via containers for Azure Functions Flex Consumption is now in preview. 

Previously, Flex Consumption apps ran in a Microsoft-managed worker environment that customers couldn’t extend with native executables, system libraries, or other OS-level components. Workloads with these requirements often had to be redesigned, move the dependency to a separate service, or use another hosting option. You can now build a Linux worker image that packages your function code, a supported Azure Functions language worker, language dependencies, and required OS-level software. This enables scenarios such as browser automation with Puppeteer and Chromium, PDF generation with Puppeteer Sharp, data encryption with GnuPG, and workloads that require system packages, executables, custom fonts, certificates, native libraries, drivers, or command-line tools. 

The worker-image model lets you version and promote a tested application environment by image digest and update its runtime and dependencies on your own release cycle. Azure manages and services the Functions host separately while continuing to provide trigger integration, request routing, and event-driven scaling. 

The preview currently supports .NET isolated, Python, Go, and Node.js, with additional language support planned in the following weeks. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Functions Network Troubleshooter v2
items.description:
Azure Functions Network Troubleshooter v2 is now in Public Preview. 

Network Troubleshooter v2 gives customers a top-down view of Function App dependencies across Storage, Service Bus, and Azure Files. For each supported dependency, customers can inspect connectivity status and verify whether Managed Identity is configured correctly. By bringing dependency discovery and these checks into one experience, it reduces the need to diagnose connectivity and configuration issues separately. There are no plan, region, or Managed Identity prerequisites or limitations. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Task Queues for Azure Functions durable task scheduler
items.description:
Task Queues for Azure Functions durable task scheduler are now available in public preview. Workloads sharing a task hub can have different throughput requirements and downstream service limits. Create named queues within a task hub and configure a shared actions-per-second dispatch rate for orchestration and activity work.

Select a queue by setting the DTS_TaskQueue tag to the queue’s name when starting a workflow. Teams can pace workloads and assign separate throughput budgets without changing function names. The rate controls work-item dispatch, not execution concurrency.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Fuzzy string match is available across Microsoft SQL offerings
items.description:
Fuzzy string match is now generally available across Microsoft SQL offerings, including Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instanced, SQL database in Microsoft Fabric, and SQL Server 2025. You can compare strings based on how similar or different they are, rather than relying only on exact matches. It can measure the distance between two strings, including how many changes are required to make them identical, or evaluate their similarity using different fuzzy matching algorithms.  

This feature makes it easier to work with imperfect or inconsistent real-world data. You can use fuzzy string match to help simplify data matching, cleansing, deduplication, fuzzy search, and other scenarios where traditional exact string comparisons may not be sufficient.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: MSSQL extension for Visual Studio Code performance dashboard
items.description:
The new query performance dashboard, now in public preview in the MSSQL extension for VS Code, leverages Query Store to surface performance insights, analyze trends, investigate execution plans, and optimize queries with GitHub Copilot.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: MSSQL extension for Visual Studio Code- Azure SQL Database container provisioning
items.description:
The MSSQL extension now supports the Azure SQL Database container, making it easy to create and manage a cloud-aligned local database environment directly in Visual Studio Code. With automatic runtime detection across Docker, WSL, Apple containers, Podman, and more, plus simple configuration and one-click provisioning, you can get started in seconds without manual container commands.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: MSSQL extension for Visual Studio Code - local-to-cloud deployment wizard
items.description:
The MSSQL extension now provides a guided local-to-cloud deployment experience for Azure SQL Database. You can move from a local Azure SQL Database container to the cloud directly from Visual Studio Code. The wizard supports schema-only or schema-and-data deployment, validates compatibility before deployment, and streamlines deployment to a new or existing Azure SQL Database.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Blob Storage turbo tier
items.description:
Azure Blob Storage turbo tier is now in Public Preview, bringing SSD-backed performance to performance-sensitive data in eligible Azure Blob Storage accounts. 

Designed for AI training, inference, analytics, and other demanding data workloads, turbo tier delivers high throughput and low latency for active data while allowing less-active data to remain on cost-efficient HDD-backed access tiers. Smart placement helps manage the active working set as access patterns change, while customers retain a single storage account with their data, namespace, and Blob API surface. 

Turbo tier public preview is available for eligible Azure Blob Storage LRS accounts in selected regions. Preview access is subject to regional capacity and eligibility. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Smart Tier (Azure Blob and Data Lake Storage) in Azure Government and China regions
items.description:
Announcing the GA of smart tier for Azure Blob and Data Lake Storage (ADLS) in Azure Government and China regions.

Smart tier is a fully managed and automated data tiering solution, avoiding manual tier placement for object storage standard online tiers.  

Smart tier automatically moves your data between hot, cool, and cold access tiers based on usage patterns, optimizing your costs for these access tiers automatically. New data is stored in the hot tier. Any object that isn’t accessed for 30 days is moved to the cool tier; after 90 days of inactivity, it transitions to the cold tier. If objects are accessed, they are transitioning back to the hot tier and restart their tiering cycle.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Backup for Azure Cosmos DB
items.description:
Azure Backup for Azure Cosmos DB is now generally available. Vaulted backup protects your Azure Cosmos DB accounts with immutable, long-term backups stored in a logically air-gapped backup vault, isolated from your production environment. It complements native continuous backups, which provide up to 35 days of operational recovery, by adding retention of up to 10 years for compliance, audit and ransomware recovery. 

With vaulted backup you get WORM immutability, soft delete, multi-user authorization, Azure RBAC and encryption with customer-managed keys, all managed centrally alongside your other Azure Backup workloads. 

New since public preview: 

  • Daily incremental backups with a weekly full backup, for a 1-day RPO 
  • Support for accounts with up to 2,500 physical partitions (about 125 TB) 
  • Cross-region restore to the Azure paired region, in addition to cross-subscription restore 
  • Availability in all Azure public cloud regions 
  • Auto-heal retries of scheduled backups that fail because of transient issues 

Supported for NoSQL and MongoDB (RU-based) accounts with continuous backup enabled. Get started today from Resiliency in the Azure portal or with the Azure CLI. 

Learn more: 

  • Documentation 
  • Tutorial 
  • Pricing details 
  • Pricing calculator

items.title: Generally Available: Database Hub in Microsoft Fabric
items.description:
Database Hub in Microsoft Fabric is a unified experience for discovering, managing, monitoring, and optimizing databases across SQL Server, Azure SQL, PostgreSQL, Azure Cosmos DB, and Fabric SQL. By bringing AI-powered insights and agents into a single control plane, Database Hub simplifies database operations and helps you modernize your data estate.

Learn more.
