items.title: Public Preview: Migrate Oracle databases to Azure HorizonDB using Azure Database Migration Service
items.description:
Azure Database Migration Service now supports Oracle-to-Azure HorizonDB data migrations. You can configure source and target connections, select the schemas to migrate, initiate data transfer, and track migration progress through a single experience—without having to build and manage custom data-movement processes.

After converting your Oracle schema using your preferred schema-conversion tools, you can use Azure Database Migration Service to migrate your data to Azure HorizonDB. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: AI Assisted Oracle-to-PostgreSQL Application Code Migration
items.description:
We provide a plugin with AI-assisted skills to help you convert application code from Oracle to PostgreSQL, enabling applications to work with Azure Database for PostgreSQL.

The plugin can be consumed through GitHub Copilot CLI or Visual Studio Code. Customers using tools such as Modernize CLI can also leverage these skills directly within their existing modernization workflows.

The skills help you identify Oracle-specific dependencies and generate proposed code changes to support PostgreSQL compatibility. Developers can review and validate the changes before accepting them.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Application Gateway advanced routing rules
items.description:
Azure Application Gateway advanced routing rules is now available in public preview. Advanced routing rules enables you to create flexible, condition-based routing logic using HTTP request attributes, extending Application Gateway routing beyond traditional path-based routing. 

You can define routing conditions based on HTTP headers, query strings, client IP addresses, HTTP methods, and request paths, and route matching requests to different backend pools. Rules support priority-based evaluation, exact-value and pattern matching, and default routing when no rule matches. 

Advanced routing rules enables scenarios such as A/B testing and canary deployments, API versioning, multi-tenant applications, traffic segmentation, and routing requests to different application backends based on request characteristics. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure DocumentDB elasticity—query from any node
items.description:
You can now send a query to any node in a multi-shard Azure DocumentDB cluster. The node can handle the query locally or route it to the shard or shards that contain the data. In effect, the nodes in a multi-shard cluster function as a router, being fully shard aware, with the ability to either serve the requests locally, route the request to the appropriate shard containing the data, or route a query across multiple shards, gather the results, and present them as one.  

This optimization guarantees performance regardless of the number of shards in a cluster and the size of the shards. For both 1x and 100x of steady state request volume, querying from any node ensures consistent performance at any scale.   

Previously, request routing relied on a single coordinator. Now, every node can route requests to the appropriate shards.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure SQL updates for mid-November 2026
items.description:
In mid-November 2026, the following updates and enhancements were made to Azure SQL:  

  • In SSMS, the new Create and Apply wizards make it simpler to create and use .dacpac and .bacpac files. The new feature consolidates and replaces the various data-tier application-related wizards with a modern, guided experience.
  • With Transparent Data Encryption (TDE), you can now temporarily halt the encryption scan on a database (suspending) and subsequently re-enable it (resuming) from the point of suspension. Suspend and resume help reduce the resource load of the TDE encryption scan, minimizing its impact on user workloads, database maintenance, and other operations. You can suspend the scan during periods of high activity and resume it when sufficient resources are available
  • Configure and lock time-based immutability for your Azure SQL Managed Instance LTR backups. Additionally, you can enable or remove legal holds on existing LTR backups to apply immutability for legal or audit purposes.
  • AI assisted query performance tuning helps you find and fix slow SQL queries. The Agent analyzes query plans and recommends query rewrites, query hints, and missing indexes, backing each recommendation by evidence and validation. 
  • Bring your own model (BYOM) to GitHub Copilot in SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS). Connect to a Microsoft Foundry deployment or another supported provider to use models that fit your workflow and organizational requirements, without leaving SSMS.
  • GitHub Copilot in SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) 22.12.1 introduces a new chat experience powered by the GitHub Copilot SDK, the same foundation used in GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio and other GitHub Copilot experiences. 
  • Preserve your open query tabs and unsaved edits when you close SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) and restore them the next time you open it.

Learn more:

  • SSMS Create and Apply wizards  

  • Transparent Data Encryption
  • Configure and lock time-based immutability Azure SQL Managed Instance LTR backups
  • AI assisted query performance
  • BYOM to GitHub Copilot in SQL Server Management Studio
  • SSMS 22.12.1 introduces new chat
  • Preserve open query tabs

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Files NFS shares on HDD
items.description:
Azure Files now supports NFS shares on HDD in public preview, expanding beyond the existing SSD offering with a cost-effective, fully managed option for Linux workloads such as general-purpose applications, shared datasets, and backups where cost efficiency is the priority.

Key benefits:

  • Align storage spending with workload needs: Choose HDD for cost-sensitive data and SSD for performance-sensitive application data.

  • Retain familiar NFS access: Move Linux workloads from on-premises file servers and NAS environments to a fully managed service.

  • Configure capacity and performance independently: Provision capacity, IOPS, and throughput to match workload requirements with Provisioned v2 billing.

To get started, complete the NFS HDD signup survey to request access. For questions or feedback, contact azfilespreview@microsoft.com.

Learn more:

  • Azure Files NFS learning documentation
  • NFS HDD signup survey

items.title: Generally Available: Symmetric keys on Azure Key Vault Premium
items.description:
Building on the public preview introduced in July 2026, this release enables customers and partners to use symmetric encryption capabilities with the oct-HSM key type and the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) algorithm directly within Azure Key Vault Premium for production workloads. 

Customers can use AES algorithms to encrypt, decrypt, wrap, and unwrap data while continuing to benefit from Azure-managed security, compliance, and operational controls.

AES algorithms with 256-bit keys are aligned with CNSA 2.0 requirements and can help organizations prepare for post-quantum cryptography readiness scenarios.

Key benefits include: 

  • Centralized key management: Securely manage symmetric keys through Azure Key Vault Premium. 
  • Hardware-backed key protection: Support for oct-HSM symmetric keys. 
  • AES cryptographic operations: Support for encryption, decryption, key wrapping, and unwrapping. 
  • Production readiness: Ready with the performance, scalability, and reliability required for production workloads. 
  • Simplified integration: Integrate symmetric key management with existing Azure security workflows. 
  • Consistent security controls: Benefit from Azure-managed security, compliance, and operational capabilities. 
Learn more:
  • Learn about keys
  • Read the documentation

items.title: Generally Available: Azure HorizonDB
items.description:
Azure HorizonDB is Microsoft’s next-generation, fully-managed, cloud-native PostgreSQL service designed for high-performance, AI-driven, and large-scale workloads. Currently generally available, it targets scenarios that require ultra-low latency, high scalability, and built-in AI capabilities for demanding workloads.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Bring-your-own image and Cosmos DB MCP server in Azure Connector Namespace hosted MCP​
items.description:
Azure Connector Namespace’s hosted MCP server capability gives AI agents access to tools without requiring developers to build and operate a separate hosting stack. The platform provisions and manages the hosting infrastructure and provides Microsoft Entra ID authentication, access controls, monitoring integration, and more. This helps teams focus on the tools and data their agents need rather than the operational work of hosting remote MCP servers. 

Connector Namespace brings two new features to hosted MCP: Bring-your-own container image and a ready-to-deploy Azure Cosmos DB MCP server:

  • Bring your own image: Host a custom MCP server. Reuse existing tools or expose business-specific capabilities to AI agents.

  • Cosmos DB MCP server: Deploy a prebuilt MCP server that lets agents discover databases and containers and query Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL. 

These new capabilities give developers more choice in how they bring MCP servers to Azure: bring your own server when you need flexibility, or start from a catalog server when you want a ready-to-use integration.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Managed Connectors in Azure Functions
items.description:
Managed connectors in Azure Functions are now generally available, enabling developers to build event-driven applications that react to events and take actions across Microsoft 365, SaaS, and business systems using the familiar Azure Functions programming model. Managed connectors, provided through the Azure Connector Namespace, wrap service-specific APIs and handle authentication, webhooks, retries, and more, so developers can focus on their application logic while Azure manages the underlying connections and integration infrastructure.

Developers can build with C#, Python, and Node.js and use connector triggers together with strongly typed Connector SDK clients for a wide range of services including Outlook, SharePoint, and Dataverse, as well as Salesforce, ServiceNow, and many other third-party systems. Built through close collaboration between Azure Connector Namespace and Azure Functions, managed connectors are integrated directly into the Functions programming and runtime experience. Functions support both webhook and polling trigger models with automatic scaling, giving developers flexibility in how applications receive and process events.

Managed connectors work alongside existing Azure Functions triggers and bindings, so developers can add integrations incrementally to new or existing applications. This makes it possible to combine business-system events with custom code, Azure services, and AI capabilities while continuing to use the deployment, scaling, and monitoring experience developers already use with Azure Functions.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Build with Azure SQL Database container locally without an Azure subscription or credit card
items.description:
You can now build and test applications using Azure SQL Database container, which runs the same Azure SQL Database engine locally that you run in the cloud. It’s free for local dev and CI, with no Azure subscription or credit card required.  

This cross-platform developer experience supports both x64 and ARM and integrates with Visual Studio Code, SSMS, Docker, native container hosts, and dev containers for a simple, consistent development workflow.  

ARM support for full text, poly base, and extensibility in Azure SQL Database container will come soon.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Transparent data encryption (TDE) in Azure SQL Database AES keys
items.description:
You can now use AES-256 keys stored in Azure Key Vault Premium or Managed HSM as TDE protectors, providing an alternative to RSA keys for protecting data at rest. While RSA may remain secure against today’s classical computing capabilities, advances in quantum computing could eventually pose a risk. AES-256 keys are considered more resistant to known quantum-computing threats than current asymmetric algorithms such as RSA. This update helps you build greater crypto agility into your platform and take practical steps toward post-quantum readiness.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Encryption at rest with customer-managed keys in Azure HorizonDB
items.description:
Customer-managed keys (CMK) for encryption at rest are now available in public preview for Azure HorizonDB.   

By default, Azure HorizonDB uses service\-managed keys (SMK) to encrypt data at rest, with Azure managing the encryption keys on your behalf. With CMK, you can instead control the key encryption key (KEK) used to protect your data by managing it in your own Azure Key Vault or Azure Key Vault Managed HSM.  

CMKs provide greater control over your encryption key lifecycle and can help you meet your organization’s security and compliance requirements. With CMK, you can: 

  • Control access to encrypted data, including revoking key access to make the Azure HorizonDB database inaccessible. 

  • Manage the key lifecycle, including key rotation, in accordance with your organization’s compliance policies. 

  • Centrally manage and organize encryption keys in Azure Key Vault. 

  • Support separation of duties across security officers, database administrators, and system administrators. 

 Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure HorizonDB Generic Log Analytics Integration
items.description:
Azure HorizonDB now supports integration with Azure Monitor diagnostic settings, enabling you to send database logs and diagnostic data to Azure Log Analytics. This provides a centralized way to query and analyze database activity, troubleshoot issues, and monitor your HorizonDB environment alongside other Azure resources.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Build Knowledge Graphs with AI pipeline in Azure HorizonDB
items.description:
Build connected, context-rich graph applications directly from your PostgreSQL data with AI pipelines in Azure HorizonDB. The new knowledge graph capability uses AI to identify entities, relationships, and properties from source data and construct a queryable graph, reducing the custom extraction, transformation, and graph-loading code typically required to get started. Configurable watermark-based incremental processing handles new source data as it arrives without rebuilding the entire graph.  

Once created, the knowledge graph enables applications to answer multi-hop questions that are difficult to resolve through keyword or vector search alone, such as how customers, transactions, incidents, assets, or documents are connected. You can combine semantic retrieval with graph relationships to build more contextual recommendations, accelerate investigations and root-cause analysis, and return traceable evidence explaining how an answer or conclusion was reached.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Migrate Oracle databases to Azure Database for PostgreSQL using Azure Database Migration Service
items.description:
Azure Database Migration Service now supports offline data migrations from Oracle to Azure Database for PostgreSQL servers. You can configure source and target connections, select the schemas to migrate, start the data transfer, and track migration status through a single experience instead of building and managing custom data-movement processes.  

After converting your Oracle schema with your preferred schema-conversion tools, you can use Azure Database Migration Service to transfer your data to Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Application Gateway confidential compute support
items.description:
Azure Application Gateway confidential compute helps organizations protect sensitive data not only in transit, but also while the gateway processes it. By running the Application Gateway data plane in a confidential computing environment, decrypted request and response data receives hardware-backed protection while being inspected and routed. 

Organizations can extend confidential computing to the application delivery layer while retaining managed capabilities including TLS termination, WAF, Layer 7 routing, Layer 4 proxying, load balancing, and observability. This is particularly useful for confidential web applications, APIs, AI applications, and regulated workloads that require stronger protection for sensitive data in use.

The add-on is available for Standard V2 and WAF V2 SKUs. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Improved Apache AGE graph query and ingestion performance on Azure HorizonDB
items.description:
Azure HorizonDB introduces substantial Apache AGE performance improvements for querying and building knowledge graphs. Enhanced query planning and optimized graph joins accelerate eligible read queries, while faster duplicate detection and improved memory management make ingestion using `MERGE` more efficient.

Benchmark results include: 

  • Up to 3,900× faster short graph lookups: In LDBC SNB tests with approximately 9 million vertices and 53 million edges, listing a person’s friends improved from approximately 1.8 seconds to 0.46 milliseconds. Selected complex queries improved by up to 512×. 
  • About 190× faster `MERGE` ingestion: Processing one million inputs with 100,000 distinct vertices improved from 906 seconds to 4.8 seconds. 
  • 83% lower sampled peak backend memory usage: In a separate 10-million-input test, memory usage fell from approximately 65.2 GiB to 11.0 GiB. 

Both read-query optimizations are enabled by default. Statistics-aware property estimates require explicitly creating property statistics and running `ANALYZE`. Performance gains vary by query, dataset, and configuration. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure SQL Database container provisioning in SQL Server Management Studio
items.description:
Now in public preview, you can provision an Azure SQL Database development environment in seconds directly from SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), with no Azure subscription, credit card, or existing database required.

Azure SQL Database container brings the Azure SQL Database engine to your local machine in a container. You can build and test applications locally and in CI against the same Azure SQL Database engine you use in the cloud, with a free local development experience available within SSMS.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Microsoft Foundry Support for Business Applications in Work IQ
items.description: Business Applications in Work IQ helps developers build business-connected agents faster in Microsoft Foundry, reducing custom integration work and turning enterprise data into actionable workflows. Organizations gain more value from their existing business applications while maintaining customer permissions and environment controls.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Multicloud Interconnect new cloud service provider support
items.description:
Announcing the general availability of Azure Multicloud Interconnect, a managed service that provides private connectivity between Azure and supported cloud providers, with Google Cloud Platform now available in public preview and Amazon Web Services in general availability. 

As organizations increasingly distribute applications, data, AI services, and business-critical workloads across multiple clouds, establishing and operating cloud-to-cloud connectivity can become complex and operationally intensive. Azure Multicloud Interconnect helps simplify this experience by providing a managed connectivity solution that reduces deployment complexity while delivering resilient private, high-performance connectivity between Azure and supported cloud environments. 

With Azure Multicloud Interconnect, you can deploy a multicloud connection directly from the Azure portal, select your cloud provider, region, and bandwidth, and onboard your environment through a guided experience. Once provisioned, you can connect Azure virtual networks and supported cloud-provider virtual networks through a private cloud-to-cloud connection, helping streamline operations and accelerate multicloud deployments. 

Key highlights: 

  • Managed private connectivity between Azure and supported cloud providers 
  • Simplified deployment and onboarding 
  • Built-in resiliency designed for mission-critical workloads 

Learn more:  

  • Read the documentation  
  • Read the announcement blog

items.title: Generally Available: Azure HorizonDB Auditing
items.description:
Azure HorizonDB now supports database auditing with the pgAudit extension. You can capture selected PostgreSQL database activities, including data access, modifications, role changes, and DDL operations, and send audit logs to Azure Monitor Log Analytics through diagnostic settings for centralized querying and analysis.

This capability helps organizations improve visibility into database activity and support security, governance, and compliance scenarios.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure HorizonDB Monitoring via Alerts
items.description:
Azure HorizonDB now supports Azure Monitor alerts, enabling you to proactively monitor your database environment and receive notifications when specified conditions are met. You can create alert rules based on HorizonDB metrics, configure thresholds, and take action when potential performance, availability, or resource utilization issues are detected. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available:  Azure HorizonDB now integrates with Azure Advisor
items.description:
Azure HorizonDB now integrates with Azure Advisor to provide personalized recommendations that help you optimize your database environment. Azure Advisor analyzes your HorizonDB resources and surfaces actionable guidance to help improve reliability, performance, security, and operational efficiency

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Unified Model API in Azure API Management
items.description:
Azure API Management now offers the Unified Model API, a standardized way to connect applications to AI models from multiple providers without managing different API interfaces and integration requirements.

Building applications with multiple AI models often requires developers to accommodate provider-specific APIs, SDKs, and request formats. The Unified Model API removes this complexity by translating requests and responses between a common API format, such as OpenAI Chat Completions, and supported model providers, including OpenAI and Anthropic.

This capability enables organizations to:

  • Accelerate AI application development: Integrate with multiple model providers using a single API interface and familiar development tools.
  • Enable model choice and portability: Adopt new models, switch providers, and implement failover strategies with minimal application changes.
  • Maintain consistent governance: Secure, monitor, and manage model traffic through a centralized API management platform, regardless of the underlying provider.

With the Unified Model API, organizations can evolve their AI architectures as model capabilities and business requirements change, while maintaining a consistent developer experience and centralized control.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Connector Namespace
items.description:
Azure Connector Namespace is now generally available, providing a fully managed integration service that enables developers to connect applications and AI agents to hundreds of Microsoft, SaaS, and enterprise systems using prebuilt, reusable connectors. Developers can access connectors from Azure Functions, Azure Container Apps, and custom applications through familiar SDKs and HTTP APIs. 

Building integrations across business systems often requires developers to manage authentication, credentials, API clients, event handling, and retry logic. Azure Connector Namespace simplifies this complexity by providing a consistent programming model while managing the underlying integration infrastructure, helping teams build and scale connected applications faster. 

With Azure Connector Namespace, customers can: 

  • Accelerate application development: Connect to hundreds of business systems using prebuilt connectors and SDKs for .NET, Node.js, and Python, without writing and maintaining custom API integration code. 

  • Simplify integration management: Centralize connections and credentials while offloading authentication, credential rotation, polling, webhooks, retries, and throttling to a managed Azure service. 

  • Build AI agents with enterprise tools: Expose connectors as MCP tools and deploy managed MCP servers, enabling AI agents to securely interact with business applications and data without custom tool implementations. 

  • Integrate across Azure compute: Reuse connectors and connections across Azure Functions, Container Apps, App Service, and custom applications without requiring a workflow engine. 

Azure Connector Namespace helps organizations build integrations, automation solutions, and AI-powered applications faster while reducing development complexity and operational overhead. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure API Management Premium v2
items.description:
Azure API Management Premium v2 is now available in 35 Azure regions, giving organizations greater flexibility to deploy and scale enterprise API workloads across more geographic locations. 

With this expanded regional availability, customers have more options to deploy API Management closer to their applications and users while meeting regional deployment and infrastructure requirements. 

Customers can create Premium v2 instances using the Azure portal, REST API, Bicep, or Azure Resource Manager (ARM) templates. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Microsoft Agent 365 integration with Azure API Management and Azure AI Gateway
items.description:
The integration between Microsoft Agent 365 and Azure API Management is now generally available, enabling organizations to centrally govern AI agents and MCP tools while enforcing security and access policies at runtime through Azure API Management and Azure AI Gateway. 

As organizations deploy more AI agents, managing access to MCP servers and tools, enforcing security policies, and monitoring agent activity becomes increasingly complex. This integration connects centralized governance in Microsoft Agent 365 with runtime enforcement in Azure API Management and Azure AI Gateway, helping organizations maintain visibility and control as agent adoption scales. 

With this integration, customers can: 

  • Discover and manage agent resources centrally: Automatically discover supported gateways and MCP servers registered in Azure API Management and Azure AI Gateway, creating a centralized inventory in Microsoft Agent 365. 

  • Enforce consistent access policies: Define governance policies in Microsoft Agent 365 and enforce access controls at runtime through Azure API Management and Azure AI Gateway, including server-level and individual tool-level blocking. 

  • Monitor and investigate agent activity: Gain visibility into agent-to-tool interactions and tool usage to support auditing, compliance, and security investigations. 

  • Protect agent interactions: Use Microsoft Defender and Microsoft Purview capabilities to help detect security threats and sensitive-information risks in supported tool requests and responses.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure AI Gateway
items.description:
Azure AI Gateway, previously available as the AI Gateway tier of API Management, is now generally available as a fully managed Azure service for connecting users, applications, and agents to AI models and MCP tools across providers.

Platform teams can centralize authentication and authorization, enforce policies, route calls across providers, monitor usage, and attribute and control costs without managing gateway infrastructure.

As AI adoption scales, developers need the flexibility to build with models and tools across providers, while platform teams need consistent security, governance, and visibility across AI interactions. Azure AI Gateway brings these capabilities together in one place, helping organizations accelerate AI development while maintaining control.

With Azure AI Gateway, customers can:

  • Accelerate AI development: Give developers easy access to AI models and MCP tools across providers through a single gateway. Simplify integrations with client-stable model aliases, choose models for the prompt with intelligent model selection, route across model deployments using priorities and weights, optimize cost and latency with session affinity, and increase reliability with automatic failover.

  • Govern and observe AI interactions: Centralize authentication and authorization, curate models and tools available to users and agents, apply content safety guardrails, and gain visibility into usage, performance, errors, and traces.

  • Control AI spend: Monitor and attribute token consumption and estimated costs across users, teams, applications, and agents. Enforce budgets, quotas, and rate limits to keep AI spending within defined limits.

Azure AI Gateway integrates with Microsoft Foundry, Microsoft Agent 365, Microsoft Entra ID, and Azure Application Insights helping organizations build on their existing Azure investments to extend security, governance, and observability across their AI applications and agents.

Customers can get started with 10,000 free gateway requests per subscription each month, with usage-based pricing as their needs grow.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Red Hat OpenShift with hosted control planes
items.description:
Today, we are excited to announce the general availability of Microsoft Azure Red Hat OpenShift with hosted control planes. This new deployment option separates the OpenShift control plane from the worker nodes running your applications. The control plane runs as a fully managed service in a Microsoft-managed Azure subscription. 

Azure Red Hat Openshift with hosted control planes helps organizations accelerate application modernization, increase developer velocity, streamline operations, and strengthen security while maintaining the familiar OpenShift experience jointly engineered and supported by Microsoft and Red Hat. Azure Red Hat OpenShift with standard architecture remains fully supported.

Azure Red Hat OpenShift with hosted control planes also supports Red Hat OpenShift 5, helping customers adopt the latest Red Hat OpenShift capabilities on Azure with an integrated support experience.

Key capabilities at general availability

  • Provision clusters faster: Clusters with hosted control planes provision in approximately 15 to 20 minutes.
  • Create clusters through a familiar Azure experience: Create and configure clusters directly in the Azure portal, or use the Azure CLI, ARM templates, or Bicep, to provision clusters as part of automated, infrastructure-as-code workflows.
  • Maintain control of encryption keys: Every cluster encrypts its OS disks with customer-managed keys, allowing you to provide and control the keys used to protect your data.
  • Use your preferred identity provider: Configure your own identity provider to authenticate and authorize administrators and users, helping you apply consistent access policies across your environment.
  • Manage clusters with greater consistency: With Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes 5, you can create, upgrade, modify, and delete hosted control plane clusters from the Advanced Cluster Management console and apply preconfigured governance policies, bringing these clusters into a single view with the rest of your Red Hat OpenShift and Kubernetes estate for centralized governance and observability. 
  • Deploy closer to your applications and users: Generally available in 8 regions globally - UK South, Canada Central, Australia East, Switzerland North, Brazil South, Central India, US East 2, WestEurope. More regions to follow post GA.

Learn more:

  • Watch the interactive demo
  • Read the documentation

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Monitor traces and Trace Analytics
items.description:
You can now analyze and compare thousands of traces, isolate the transactions that matter, and move from trends to root cause with advanced distributed tracing within Azure Monitor Application Insights.

Azure Monitor traces (preview) provides a dedicated trace store for distributed traces. It assembles related spans into complete traces at ingestion time, so you can analyze end-to-end transactions across your services and dependencies.
Use Trace Analytics to search and analyze groups of traces. You can identify patterns in performance and failures, compare groups of transactions, and open individual traces for detailed investigation. Use trace-based metrics to power service-level indicators, dashboards, alerts and long-term trend analysis.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Monitor Health Models
items.description:
Azure Monitor Health Models is now Generally Available.  
You can now build a Azure Monitor Health Model that defines and operationalizes workload health as a first-class construct by aggregating signals across metrics, logs, and dependencies into a single, unified health state. It reduces alert noise, accelerating incident response, and improving reliability for your services.  

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Session-based authentication for Azure Blob and Data Lake Storage
items.description:
Session-based authentication is now in public preview for Azure Blob and Data Lake Storage.

Session-based authentication reduces the per-request authentication and authorization time for AI agents and applications while preserving the security controls organizations already rely on.

With session-based authentication, an agent or application authenticates once with Microsoft Entra ID, establishes a short-lived session for a container, and uses that session for subsequent reads.

Session-based authentication provides three benefits:

  • Improved performance. Identity and permissions are verified once when the session is created. Subsequent read requests to the container use that session which reduces per-request authentication and authorization latency.
  • The same least privileged access, now short-lived. Sessions use your organization’s existing permission model for least privileged access, Azure RBAC and Azure ABAC. Each session is also scoped to one container, expires after five minutes, is bound to the client that created it, and requires every request to be signed.

  • Full traceability.  Azure Storage diagnostic logs currently record the Microsoft Entra ID identity behind each request, and the same is true with sessions. With sessions, every request remains tied to the Microsoft Entra ID identity that created the session, so security teams keep visibility into which identity, human or agent, accessed what data, and when. 

This preview is available in all public regions, supports the Get Blob operation, and is available through the REST API and Azure Storage SDKs. With the SDK, enabling session-based authentication is a single client configuration option, with no changes to your application logic.

Creating a session is billed as a write transaction. Read requests made with a session are billed at the standard transaction rates for your storage account type.

Learn more: 

  • Blog  
  • Documentation

items.title: Public Preview: Centralized user authentication + JWT validation for Azure Application Gateway
items.description:
Announcing the public preview of centralized user authentication for Azure Application Gateway, along with an updated JWT validation experience. 

User authentication enables Application Gateway to sign users in with OpenID Connect before traffic reaches a web application. With centralized authentication policies, customers can configure authentication once and apply it consistently across routing rules and multiple Application Gateways. This approach helps simplify application architecture, reduce authentication code in backend applications, and provide a consistent sign-in experience across protected web apps.

As part of this centralized policy model, Application Gateway also includes an updated JWT validation experience for scenarios such as APIs and service-to-service traffic. JWT validation helps validate bearer tokens at the gateway before requests reach backend applications, supporting a more consistent security posture across applications. 

The updated JWT validation experience is a revision of the existing Application Gateway JWT validation preview. The existing preview will not move forward to general availability, and Microsoft plans to deprecate it. A separate deprecation notice will be published with the deprecation date, retirement timeline, and transition guidance. This announcement is not the formal deprecation notice.

Learn more:

  • JWT validation
  • User authentication

items.title: Public Preview: Advanced load balancing in Azure Application Gateway
items.description:
Advanced load balancing for Azure Application Gateway is now available in public preview, giving you greater control over how traffic is distributed across backends supporting different workloads, including AI applications and web traffic. New server-level algorithms and backend pool controls let you tailor traffic distribution to your application’s capacity and routing requirements. 

At the backend pool level, priority controls let you designate preferred pools, while weights let you configure the relative traffic share across eligible pools. For AI applications, you can prioritize pools hosting preferred large language model (LLM) deployments. For web applications, you can adjust traffic distribution across pools to reflect differences in backend capacity and deployment needs. Within each backend pool, Least Connections directs traffic to servers with fewer active connections, while Weighted Round Robin distributes traffic according to configured server weights. Together, these capabilities provide flexible, policy-driven traffic management for AI and web workloads.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Next-generation elastic architecture for Azure Application Gateway v2
items.description:
A next-generation elastic architecture for Azure Application Gateway v2 is now available in public preview. Built for demanding workloads and dynamic traffic patterns, it reduces provisioning time by up to 50% and autoscaling time by up to 70% compared to the current deployment tier. It also lays the foundation for higher configuration and data-plane scale limits while maintaining seamless application connectivity as gateways scale out and scale in. 

This platform upgrade is available at no additional cost. To opt in, select "Accelerated (Preview)" under Deployment tier when creating a new Application Gateway. During the preview period, the tier is available in select regions, with additional regions being added over time. Existing gateways are unaffected and will continue to operate as-is. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Decision actions in Azure Logic Apps Automation
items.description:
Decision actions are now available in public preview in Azure Logic Apps Automation, enabling developers to automate business decisions using AI without deploying or managing models.

Many business processes require judgment calls, such as classifying customer requests, routing support tickets, or assessing issue severity. Traditionally, developers rely on rigid rules or general-purpose AI models that require additional prompting and response parsing. Powered by Microsoft-Decision-1, Decision actions provide a simpler way to incorporate AI-powered decisions directly into workflows.

Three new built-in actions enable developers to:

  • Yes/No: Evaluate whether a condition is true, such as identifying refund requests.

  • Choice: Classify information into predefined categories, such as routing tickets to the appropriate team.

  • Score: Assess content against an ordered scale, such as determining issue severity.

Decision actions return structured results with probabilities and confidence information that workflows can use directly for routing, conditional execution, or human review. With fully managed AI capabilities and built-in run history, developers can build intelligent business process automation faster while maintaining visibility and control.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: New built-in Azure automation connectors in Logic Apps Automation
items.description:
New built-in connectors for Azure automation are now available in public preview in Azure Logic Apps Automation, enabling developers to automate workflows across GitHub, Azure DevOps, and Azure management services.

Automating development and cloud operations often requires connecting multiple systems to manage code, track work, monitor resources, and respond to events. These connectors simplify the process by bringing these capabilities together in a single workflow, reducing the need for custom integrations.

With the new built-in connectors, customers can:

  • Automate development workflows: Connect to GitHub, Azure DevOps Pipelines, Repos, and Boards to automate issue triage, pull request reviews, work item management, and CI/CD processes.

  • Streamline Azure operations: Use Azure Monitor Logs, Azure Resource Graph, and Azure Advisor to query operational data, discover resources, and act on recommendations.

  • Build event-driven automation: Trigger workflows from events such as new issues, pull requests, or work item updates, and combine these actions with AI agents for intelligent automation.

These connectors help organizations streamline development and operational processes while reducing manual effort and integration complexity.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Virtual network integration in Logic Apps Automation
items.description:
Virtual network (VNet) integration is now available in public preview in Azure Logic Apps Automation, enabling organizations to securely connect workflows and agents to resources within their Azure virtual networks.

As organizations automate business processes and cloud operations, workflows often need to access private databases, internal APIs, and other resources that aren't publicly accessible. VNet integration enables Logic Apps Automation environments to route outbound traffic through a customer-managed virtual network, supporting secure connectivity to private resources.

With VNet integration, customers can:

  • Connect to private resources: Enable workflows, built-in connectors, and agents to access internal APIs, databases, and Azure services through a virtual network.

  • Strengthen network security: Route outbound automation traffic through an organization's virtual network to apply existing network controls and policies.

  • Simplify configuration: Enable VNet integration when creating a Logic Apps Automation environment by selecting a virtual network and subnet.

VNet integration helps organizations extend automation to private enterprise systems while maintaining control over network connectivity and security.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Managed AI Models in Logic Apps Automation
items.description:
Managed AI Models are now available in public preview in Azure Logic Apps Automation, enabling developers to bring AI capabilities into workflows and agents without provisioning, deploying, or managing model infrastructure.

Building AI-powered automation often requires developers to configure model deployments, manage credentials, and maintain supporting infrastructure before they can begin developing workflows. Managed AI Models simplify this experience by providing ready-to-use AI models directly within Logic Apps Automation.

With Managed AI Models, customers can:

  • Accelerate AI-powered automation: Use managed models to add AI capabilities to workflows and agents without configuring or maintaining model deployments.

  • Build intelligent workflows faster: Combine AI-driven reasoning with deterministic workflow actions to automate tasks such as issue triage, content summarization, and operational analysis.

  • Reduce infrastructure complexity: Focus on building business process automation while Logic Apps Automation manages the underlying model infrastructure.

Managed AI Models help developers move from ideas to working AI-powered automations faster, while retaining the orchestration and integration capabilities of Azure Logic Apps Automation.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Enhanced developer experience in Azure Logic Apps Automation
items.description:
Azure Logic Apps Automation introduces new developer experiences that make it faster and easier to build, manage, and scale business process automation. Enhancements include a refreshed workflow designer, reusable templates, faster environment and application creation, and expanded regional availability.

As organizations scale automation, developers need intuitive tools, reusable patterns, and simplified infrastructure setup to move from ideas to production faster. These enhancements streamline the development experience while reducing setup and operational complexity.

With these improvements, customers can:

  • Build workflows faster: Use a refreshed designer with improved visual navigation, clearer branching, and streamlined editing to create and manage complex workflows.

  • Accelerate development with templates: Start with ready-to-use templates for integration, Azure operations, and agentic automation, or turn existing workflows into reusable templates that can be shared across teams.

  • Get started more quickly: Create environments and applications faster with an optimized runtime foundation that reduces infrastructure provisioning overhead.

  • Deploy across more regions: Take advantage of expanded availability across Azure public regions, with rollout underway.

These enhancements help developers build automations faster, reuse proven patterns, and scale business processes with greater flexibility.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: New integration, hybrid deployment, and observability capabilities in Azure Logic Apps
items.description:
Azure Logic Apps introduces new and enhanced capabilities to help organizations connect enterprise systems, modernize legacy integrations, and run business-critical workflows across cloud, on-premises, and hybrid environments. These updates include expanded connector support, data mapping enhancements, centralized monitoring, and greater flexibility for deploying and managing Hybrid Logic Apps.

As organizations modernize enterprise integration, they need to connect existing systems, simplify data transformation, and maintain reliable operations across diverse environments. These enhancements help reduce integration complexity while enabling organizations to build on their existing infrastructure investments.

With these updates, customers can:

  • Connect more enterprise systems: Use the HL7 connector, now generally available, to process healthcare messages. New MLLP and MSMQ connectors, available in public preview, extend connectivity for healthcare messaging and legacy enterprise systems.

  • Simplify data transformation: Use Data Mapper enhancements to streamline mapping and transformation across enterprise applications and message formats.

  • Gain centralized visibility: Monitor workflow execution and troubleshoot integrations through the new unified dashboard, available in public preview for individual Logic Apps.

  • Extend integration to hybrid environments: Use Integration Account capabilities in semi-connected environments and expand deployment flexibility with support for RKE2 and Red Hat OpenShift Kubernetes clusters.

  • Simplify hybrid operations: Automate Hybrid Logic Apps deployments through DevOps pipelines and use supported SQL Server storage options for workflow state and runtime data.

Together, these capabilities help organizations modernize enterprise integrations while maintaining flexibility, operational visibility, and control across their environments.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Infrastructure Resiliency Manager
items.description: Azure Infrastructure Resiliency Manager is now generally available, offering a unified, goal-driven experience to strengthen application resiliency across Azure. You can start resilient with zonally resilient deployment templates, assess applications at scale using Service Groups and resiliency goals, and prioritize recommendations with visibility into cost impact. Resiliency drift detection, resource and application monitoring, and built-in drills help you proactively maintain their resiliency posture, validate recoverability, and support compliance reporting. You can additionally leverage the Resiliency Agent (preview) to automatically discover application boundaries and access ready-to-run remediation scripts.

items.title: Public Preview: Microsoft Teams integration for Azure SRE Agent
items.description:
Azure SRE Agent can now take part in Microsoft Teams conversations in public preview. Engineers can start an investigation, follow up on findings, and work with the agent in one-on-one chats, group chats, channels, and meeting chats without leaving Teams. When an action requires authorization, the agent posts an approval card in the conversation. 

Administrators decide which shared conversations the agent can take part in, while existing tool policies determine whether actions are allowed, require approval, or are denied. Microsoft Entra Agent ID enables the agent’s Teams presence; managed identity and Azure role-based access control continue to govern access to Azure resources. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol support in Azure SRE Agent
items.description:
Azure SRE Agent now supports the open Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol in public preview. SRE agents can hand tasks to other agents and accept tasks from them while each agent retains its own team’s permissions. For example, an application team’s agent investigating a latency spike can ask a database team’s agent to check query performance and bring the findings back into the same investigation. 

Administrators determine which agents an SRE agent can call, approve incoming callers in the same Microsoft Entra tenant, and select which custom agent handles their requests. Connections use managed identity and do not give remote agents direct access to the caller’s tools or permissions. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Microsoft Entra Agent ID and Agent 365 for Azure SRE Agent
items.description:
Azure SRE Agent now supports Microsoft Entra Agent ID and Microsoft Agent 365 in public preview, so security and IT teams can see and govern SRE agents alongside other agents in the organization. 

Each agent can have its own Agent ID in addition to its managed identity. Teams can assign Azure roles to the Agent ID so the agent's actions appear as itself in Entra and in Azure activity logs. Through Agent 365, administrators can find SRE agents in the tenant's agent registry and monitor their activity with Microsoft Purview and Microsoft Defender. 

Learn more.

items.title: Private Preview: Slack integration for Azure SRE Agent
items.description:
Azure SRE Agent is coming to Slack in private preview. Organizations that coordinate incident response in Slack can work with the agent in the channels where responders already work, mentioning it to start or follow up on an investigation and receiving findings in the same conversation, so the wider response team can follow along without switching tools.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure DDoS Protection custom policy
items.description:
Azure DDoS Protection custom policy is now generally available, and it’s one of our most requested features. By default, machine-learning auto-tuning sets detection thresholds for each protected resource, which works well for most workloads. But latency-sensitive apps, high-throughput services, and gaming or event-driven workloads with planned spikes often need a fixed threshold. Custom policy lets you set your own for individual protocols, across Azure resources with public IP endpoints, on both Network Protection and IP Protection SKUs. 

Each policy holds one or more rules that define a protocol (TCP, UDP or TCP SYN), an inbound direction, and a packets-per-second threshold that triggers mitigation. You can link a policy to up to 1,000 resources, and you can create it first and add associations later. Setting a threshold turns off auto-tuning for that protocol only, so everything else stays machine-learning tuned. Settings now persist with your resource, so they survive workload removal or VM shutdown, and you manage them yourself without on-call support. 

Take control of how your workloads are protected.

 Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure DDoS Protection support for NAT Gateway v2 IP
items.description:
Azure DDoS Protection now covers the public IPs behind Azure NAT Gateway StandardV2, in public preview. You can protect the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses that carry your outbound internet traffic from network-layer DDoS attacks, using the same DDoS Network Protection or IP Protection you already have. There’s no new API, feature registration or appliance to manage, and no unsolicited inbound connections are opened to your gateway. 

Why it matters: 

NAT Gateway doesn’t accept inbound connections, but its public IPs are still reachable from the internet, and they’re the identity of everything behind them. Partners, SaaS providers and banks often allow-list these IPs, so anyone who learns them can aim traffic at them. Every VM in the associated subnets shares the same IPs, so a single flood can cut off API calls, partner integrations, updates and telemetry all at once. An attacker doesn’t need to reach your workloads to cause an outage, only to break their path to the internet. 

Now your outbound IPs get automatic network-layer mitigation, plus the DDoS metrics, diagnostics and alerts you already rely on. It also simplifies compliance, because policies requiring DDoS protection on all public IPs no longer need an exception for NAT Gateway. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Pod snapshot cluster extension
items.description:
Restarting a sandboxed workload means losing in-memory state and repeating costly initialization. AI environments must reload models and rebuild runtime context; other sandboxed applications must repeat Java Virtual Machine (JVM) warmup or repopulate caches. Users wait while work that was already completed runs again.

We’re introducing the Pod Snapshot cluster extension to capture a supported pod runtime state and restore it on demand, preserving memory and process state in Azure Blob instead of cold-starting. Paired with the Agent Sandbox cluster extension, it lets teams capture and restore isolated agent environments. For both agent and other supported sandboxed workloads, resuming from captured state reduces repeated initialization and the wait before work can continue.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Native AWS and Google Cloud support in Azure SRE Agent
items.description:
Azure SRE Agent now natively supports AWS and Google Cloud through built-in connectors, available in public preview. Bring operational evidence together to investigate applications and dependencies across Azure and your connected AWS or Google Cloud environments. 

The connectors use an Azure managed identity and identity federation with AWS IAM roles and Google Cloud Workload Identity Federation. There's no need to manage AWS access keys or Google Cloud service account keys, build custom connectors, or host MCP servers. 

Use separate connections for multiple AWS accounts, or one Google Cloud connection across projects where the federated identity has permissions. Ask in natural language, or automate investigations with incident response plans, scheduled tasks, and workflows. 

Cloud IAM, SRE Agent run modes, and tool approvals govern access and operations. Supported activity can be audited in AWS CloudTrail and Google Cloud Audit Logs when logging is configured. 

Learn more: 

  • AWS connector guide   
  • Google Cloud connector guide

items.title: Public Preview: Windows Server 2028
items.description:
Windows Server 2028, the next Long-Term Servicing Channel (LTSC) release of Windows Server, is now in public preview. It brings together security, virtualization, hybrid cloud management, and hybrid intelligence investments to support mission-critical workloads across datacenters, edge, and cloud environments.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Rename Server in Azure Database for MySQL
items.description:
We’re excited to announce the general availability of server renaming for Azure Database for MySQL. Now you can update the name of an existing server instance without needing to recreate the server, migrate data, or disrupt applications. You can adopt clear, consistent naming without interrupting applications. Server renaming provides a near zero-downtime path to a new hostname of the server.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Compute Spot plus
items.description:
Azure Compute Spot plus, now in public preview, is an enhanced tier of Azure Spot Virtual Machines, bringing greater runtime consistency and earlier eviction signals to interruption-tolerant workloads.

Standard Spot suits highly resilient workloads focused on savings. Spot plus offers more predictability and time to respond to interruptions.

Key capabilities:

  • Targets at least 60 minutes of runtime on a best-effort basis, while remaining evictable
  • If Azure evicts a Spot plus VM to reclaim capacity within the first 60 minutes, you aren't charged for that VM's usage
  • Up to 2 minutes' eviction notice to checkpoint or drain work
  • Rebalance notifications, typically 30 seconds to 15 minutes ahead, signal elevated eviction risk

Spot plus costs more than standard Spot and remains well below pay-as-you-go pricing. Deploy through the Compute API, ARM templates, Azure portal, Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell and Azure SDKs, on single-instance VMs and Virtual Machine Scale Sets with Flexible or Uniform orchestration.

Register your subscription for the Spot plus preview feature and deploy a VM or scale set with SpotPlus priority using API version 2026-04-01 or later.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Ebsv6 and Ebdsv6
items.description:
We’re excited to announce the general availability of Azure Ebsv6 and Ebdsv6 VMs, powered by 5th Gen Intel® Xeon® processors and Azure Boost, delivering enhanced storage performance for I/O-intensive workloads.

Designed for relational databases, in-memory analytics, and data warehousing, these remote storage optimized VMs provide improved compute and storage performance over the previous generation.

Key benefits include:

  • Enhanced storage performance: Up to 800K IOPS and 12.5 GB/s remote storage throughput with Azure Boost, supporting Premium SSD v2 and Ultra Disk.

  • Improved efficiency: Up to 15% higher remote storage performance per vCPU and 15–30% improved CPU performance.

  • High scalability: Up to 96 vCPUs and 768 GiB memory, with 192-vCPU sizes and up to 1.8 TB memory coming soon.

  • Flexible configurations: Choose Ebsv6 for memory-intensive workloads or Ebdsv6 with local NVMe temporary storage.

  • Enhanced security and connectivity: Up to 200 Gbps networking and Intel Total Memory Encryption enabled by default.

Ebsv6 and Ebdsv6 VMs are now generally available across multiple Azure regions.

Learn more:

  • Announcement blog
  • Ebdsv6 VM series documentation
  • Ebsv6 VM series documentation

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Linux 4.0
items.description:
Azure Linux 4.0 is being introduced as part of Microsoft Ignite. The general availability of Azure Linux 4.0 for Azure Virtual Machines and VM Scale Sets is Microsoft's first-party open-source Linux distribution purpose-built for Azure. It brings a modernized stack — including Linux kernel 6.18 LTS, dnf5 package manager, glibc 2.42, OpenSSL 3.5, and Python 3.14 — optimized for Azure compute, storage, and networking. It delivers faster VM startup and provisioning with a reduced package footprint and a security-first design. 

 Key highlights: 

  • Azure-tuned kernel — Linux 6.18 LTS with improved Hyper-V integration, GPU/AI accelerator support, and new hardware drivers 
  • Secure by default — Secure Boot, Trusted Launch, SELinux support, kernel hardening, and SBOMs published with target SLSA Level 3 
  • Minimal footprint — Ships only the packages required for cloud workloads, reducing attack surface from day one 
  • No additional OS licensing cost — Included with Azure compute; no separate OS licensing fees or support contracts 
  • Microsoft-owned supply chain — From kernel to CVE response, enabling fast-track Critical/High CVE patches with monthly security updates 
  • Predictable lifecycle —full support with LTS kernel and annual HWE kernel updates for new hardware platforms 
  • Container images — Base, and distroless images available on Microsoft Container Registry (MCR)

Learn more: 

  • Ignite 2026 blog 
  • GitHub 
  • Documentation

items.title: Generally Available: Azure HorizonDB System Managed Maintenance Window
items.description:
Azure HorizonDB supports system-managed maintenance for planned service upgrades.With system-managed maintenance, Azure HorizonDB automatically performs planned upgrades on your cluster without requiring you to configure or manage a maintenance schedule.

This helps keep your cluster secure, reliable, and up to date while reducing the operational overhead of managing routine service maintenance.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure DDoS Protection peacetime telemetry
items.description:
Azure DDoS Protection peacetime telemetry is now in public preview. Customers can now see the traffic reaching their protected public IP addresses during normal operation, not only while a DDoS mitigation is active. 

Previously, outside an active mitigation, a protected public IP address showed only its mitigation-trigger metrics. With peacetime telemetry, the existing incoming DDoS traffic metrics (total, TCP, SYN, UDP and other traffic) show data during normal operation. 

Customers can use this data to understand normal traffic patterns, compare everyday traffic with mitigation triggers, create Azure Monitor metric alerts with workload-specific thresholds, and test dashboards and alerts without simulating an attack. 

Peacetime telemetry works automatically for public IP addresses protected by DDoS Network Protection or DDoS IP Protection, with no registration and no new metric names. Viewing the metrics doesn't require Log Analytics or diagnostic settings, and protection and mitigation behavior don't change. There's no additional cost beyond existing DDoS Protection pricing; standard Azure Monitor charges apply to alert rules. During the preview, peacetime telemetry is available in the Azure public cloud. 

Learn more: 

  • Read about peacetime telemetry availability 
  • Set up traffic-condition alerts during peacetime

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Policy support for Azure HorizonDB
items.description:
Azure Policy support for Azure HorizonDB is now available in preview, helping you apply governance and observability standards consistently across your HorizonDB deployments.

With the new built-in policy, you can automatically deploy diagnostic settings for Azure HorizonDB clusters to a Log Analytics workspace when the required configuration is missing. This helps you establish consistent monitoring across your HorizonDB environments while reducing the need for manual configuration.

Azure Policy provides a centralized way to define and enforce organizational standards across Azure resources, making it easier to govern HorizonDB deployments at scale.

Learn more.

items.title: Private Preview: Project Nova
items.description: Project NOVA enables independent verification of specific claims without revealing the underlying data. Across regulated industries, organizations need to establish trust while protecting confidential information. Project Nova explores how zero-knowledge proofs can enable privacy-preserving transactions, interoperability, and regulatory assurance across organizational boundaries. In financial services, zero-knowledge proofs could enable cross-chain settlement by verifying transaction conditions across networks, support selective disclosure of sensitive information, and provide regulators with independent assurance of compliance without exposing underlying records. Beyond financial services, healthcare organizations could verify patient eligibility without sharing medical histories; AI systems could prove defined computations without exposing sensitive inputs; and supply chains could demonstrate compliance or product provenance without revealing confidential supplier relationships.

items.title: Private Preview: Azure confidential VMs on 5th Gen AMD EPYC processors (DCasv7 and ECasv7 series)
items.description: Azure's next-generation confidential VMs, the DCasv7, DCadsv7, DCalsv7, DCaldsv7, ECasv7 and ECadsv7 series, are now in private preview. Built on 5th Gen AMD EPYC processors with AMD SEV-SNP, they protect data while it's being processed by isolating each VM in hardware from the hypervisor, host operators and other tenants. Customers can move sensitive, regulated workloads to the cloud without changing their code. General-purpose, low-memory and memory-optimized sizes are available, with or without local disk, so customers can match price and performance to each workload while meeting privacy, compliance and sovereignty requirements.

items.title: Public Preview: Sovereign Control Panel
items.description:
Sovereign Control Panel is now available in Public Preview. Sovereign Control Panel is an Azure portal experience designed to help organizations assess and continuously monitor their sovereignty posture, understand the evidence behind identified gaps, and take guided action to address them. From a centralized experience, customers can apply sovereignty controls, prioritize remediation recommendations, and track improvements across their existing Azure estate, reducing the need to manually assemble information across tools and teams for each assessment. 

Learn more.

items.title: Announcing: Production Touch Ledger (PTL) Assessment Report
items.description:
The Production Touch Ledger (PTL) Assessment Report is now available. Capgemini, an independent third party, has validated the design of PTL for its ability to preserve the completeness, tamper-evidence, and non-repudiation of production-access records. This provides customers with independent assessment of PTL’s capabilities rather than solely relying on Microsoft’s claims. PTL, launched with phased rollout in the EU Data Boundary, provides organizations a verifiable record of when and how Microsoft personnel access the in-scope production systems that host their workloads. Every access record is written to Azure Confidential Ledger, making the record tamper-evident: once an entry is recorded, any attempt to alter or remove it can be detected. Security, compliance, and risk teams can use the PTL Assessment Report as independent evidence in regulatory reviews, internal audits, and customer access conversations.

Learn more:
  • Download the Assessment Report
  • Production Touch Ledger Documentation

items.title: Generally Available: Discover Data Guardian from Sovereign Control Panel
items.description:
Customers can now discover Data Guardian directly from the Sovereign Control Panel, now in Public Preview. Data Guardian provides enhanced operational oversight of qualifying remote access by Microsoft engineers to in-scope production systems in the EU data boundary. Access is subject to monitoring by authorized EU-resident personnel from a trusted partner. With this update, customers reviewing their sovereignty posture in Sovereign Control Panel can learn about Data Guardian, understand how it supports their access oversight requirements, all from the same centralized experience. This makes it easier to move from assessing posture to exploring relevant controls, without searching across separate tools and documentation. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: VM adaptive placement
items.description:
VM adaptive placement, now in public preview, helps increase Azure VM deployment success when capacity is constrained.

With a standard VM create, you specify one exact size, and the deployment fails if that size isn't available. With adaptive placement, you specify a preferred size instead. Azure deploys your preferred size when it can. If it isn't available, Azure deploys a compatible alternative with the same vCPU count, the same or newer generation, and equivalent performance.

Adaptive placement isn't a new VM type or pricing offer. You get a regular Azure VM, billed at standard rates for the deployed size, with no additional charge.

Key capabilities:

  • Replace custom retry loops and fallback lists with a placement decision Azure makes at request time
  • See both your preferred size and the deployed size on the VM
  • Use it for new VMs or update existing VMs

During preview, preferred sizes can come from the D-, E- and F-series families. Adaptive placement is for single VMs and isn't supported with Capacity Reservations, Dedicated Hosts, Availability Sets or Proximity Placement Groups. It works within your quota and isn't a capacity guarantee. Use the REST API, Azure PowerShell or the .NET and Python SDKs; the Azure portal isn't supported in preview.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Artifact Validation for VM images
items.description:
Azure Artifact Validation, in public preview, lets VM image publishers and enterprise platform teams run Azure's certification-grade quality and security checks on their images in their own Azure subscriptions, at any point in the build process.

Previously, these checks ran only when you submitted an Azure Marketplace offer in Partner Center. Now you can validate Windows and Linux images bound for Azure Marketplace, galleries or other distribution platforms, and find issues while they're still inexpensive to fix.

Key capabilities:

  • Self-service validation runs in your own subscription, with your choice of tests and timing
  • Checks for bootability, OS configuration and platform compatibility, plus malware and vulnerability scanning powered by Microsoft Defender
  • A native Azure resource with an API, so you can add validation to CI/CD pipelines as a release gate
  • Per-test results with stable error codes and clear reasons

Artifact Validation complements Azure Marketplace certification and doesn't replace it; final certification still runs through Partner Center.

Available in Central US, North Central US, South Central US, Sweden Central, Japan East and Australia East through the REST API, ARM templates and Azure SDKs.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: IBM Spectrum LSF integration with Azure Compute Fleet
items.description:
IBM Spectrum LSF integrates with Azure Compute Fleet for elastic, cost-efficient HPC workload orchestration.

The IBM LSF Resource Connector for Azure Compute Fleet provisions and releases compute capacity based on workload demand. Extend on-premises LSF environments to Azure or run LSF-managed HPC clusters in the cloud, without changing job submission workflows.

LSF manages scheduling, queues and policies, while Azure Compute Fleet provisions capacity across the VM families, sizes and purchasing options you configure.

Key capabilities:

  • Automatically provision and release Azure VMs in response to LSF job demand
  • Specify multiple VM families and sizes in one Fleet request to improve the likelihood of obtaining capacity at peak
  • Run fault-tolerant, restartable jobs on Azure Spot Virtual Machines and keep workloads that need continuity on pay-as-you-go capacity
  • Preserve existing queue hierarchies, fairshare policies and license-aware scheduling

Workloads include semiconductor design and EDA, genomics, automotive simulation, energy research and financial risk modeling.

Download the Azure Compute Fleet plugin for IBM Spectrum LSF from Azure Marketplace and follow IBM's configuration guidance.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Migrate PostgreSQL servers to Azure HorizonDB
items.description:
Azure Database Migration Service support for migrations to Azure HorizonDB is now available in public preview. You can use a guided, Azure portal–based experience to migrate supported PostgreSQL workloads to Azure HorizonDB, including Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server, self-managed PostgreSQL on Azure Virtual Machines or on-premises, Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL, Amazon Aurora for PostgreSQL, Google Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, and other compatible environments.  

The new experience helps simplify source and target connectivity, database selection, and migration monitoring, enabling your organization to modernize mission-critical and AI-ready PostgreSQL applications with a more consistent migration workflow. 


Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Migrate Azure Database for PostgreSQL to Azure HorizonDB with Azure Database Migration Service (DMS)
items.description:
Now you can migrate existing Azure Database for PostgreSQL workloads to Azure HorizonDB through a seamless, managed experience powered by Azure Database Migration Service (DMS). With this update, you can extend the DMS V2 architecture with HorizonDB as a supported PostgreSQL target, allowing you to modernize onto a high-performance, scalable PostgreSQL platform without building or operating custom migration infrastructure.  

You can initiate and manage a migration through the Azure portal or command-line interfaces. DMS validates source and target connectivity, discovers database objects, provisions isolated migration compute on demand, and orchestrates the end-to-end workflow, including initial data copy, continuous synchronization for online migrations, progress monitoring, error handling, cancellation, and planned cutover. Migration state and operation history are persisted centrally, so you and your support teams have consistent visibility throughout the lifecycle.

items.title: Limited Preview: Compute templates for Azure
items.description:
Announcing the limited preview of Azure compute templates, a new capability that simplifies virtual machine (VM) configuration management by enabling customers to define, version, and reuse standardized VM configurations across deployments.

With compute templates, customers can create a reusable configuration baseline for common VM settings, including OS, storage, and security, and store it as a versioned instance profile in Azure Compute Gallery.

Key benefits include:

  • Simplified VM deployments: Define common configurations once and reuse them across supported VM deployments.

  • Improved consistency: Reduce configuration drift and maintenance overhead through standardized, versioned configurations.

  • Flexible deployment options: Apply templates to single-instance VMs and VM adaptive placement while supporting deployment-specific settings and overrides.

  • Streamlined management: Manage reusable configurations independently of individual deployment requests.

During the limited preview, compute templates are available through REST APIs for supported single-instance VMs, including VM adaptive placement. Preview registration and subscription enablement are required. VM scale sets and Azure Compute Fleet are not currently supported.
